Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 35, verse 1:

We have touched on the surahs that begin with "Al-hamdu lillah" (All praise is due to Allah), namely: [al-Fatiha], al-An'am, al-Kahf, and Saba'. Here in Fatir, the praise in each of them has its own meaning and its own appropriateness, because man needed first to be brought into existence from nothing, then needed means of sustaining himself in this worldly life, then needed to be brought into existence again after resurrection, and likewise needs means of sustenance in the Hereafter.

Surah al-Kahf dealt with praising Allah for the method (al-manhaj).

"All praise is due to Allah, who sent down upon His servant the Book..." [al-Kahf: 1]. This is because the method is the means of sustaining man, for if the method did not make clear to people the truth and the falsehood, creation would have perished and life would not have been set right for them. As for Surah Saba', it dealt with praising Allah for His blessings in this world and in the Hereafter.

And here in Fatir: "All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers..." So He mentioned praise for all the means of sustenance: the material ones represented in the requisites of material life, and the immaterial ones represented in the method of Allah.

Praise in its absolute sense belongs to Allah, Exalted, even when it is directed to human beings, for it ultimately returns to Allah. When you praise a person, you praise him for something he has given you, and that thing is not truly his possession, nor from his own essence; rather, it is from the overflowing bounty of Allah upon him. Thus he is a conduit on behalf of Allah. And if he provides you with a deed, he provides it only by the power Allah created in him and by the limbs that were moved by Allah's creation in him. Therefore, praise in every form returns to Allah, Exalted.

Then He mentions an aspect of the praiseworthy attributes of Allah, saying: "Originator of the heavens and the earth." The meaning of "Fatir as-samawati wal-ard" is that He created them and originated them without any prior pattern to be imitated, and this is a matter deserving of praise, because Allah, Exalted, honoured man as vicegerent on earth, made him superior to the rest of the species, and honoured him with reason by which he chooses among alternatives.

Then He, glorified be He, showed that although the creation of man is wondrous, and although he is the master served by all species, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater and more magnificent than the creation of people; therefore, when He spoke of praising Allah, He mentioned the greatest and most magnificent of creatures, which are the heavens and the earth.

The "sama'" (heaven) is everything that is above you; for this reason it is applied to the clouds, for it is the "sky" from which rain descends...

As for His saying, "who made the angels messengers..." These angels were made messengers by Allah, either to the messengers among mankind, carrying to them the method of Allah, or as messengers from Him, glorified be He, for their tasks that relate to this human being. Then He described them, saying: "Possessors of wings, two, three, or four..." [Fatir: 1]. This description indicates the angels' connection with the air and the sky, and their task of ascending and descending. These wings do not follow a fixed arrangement; rather, among them is one who has two, among them one who has three, and among them one who has four, and beyond that Allah increases in creation what He wills: "He increases in creation what He wills" [Fatir: 1].

It is as though the Creator, glorified be He, is saying to us: if you have seen only two wings for a bird, do not be astonished or deny that an angel may have more than that, for it is the creation of Allah who increases in creation what He wills, and to whom belongs absolute power. The creation of Allah is not a mechanical process or moulds poured into a single shape, and the creation of Allah is not an automatic bakery that produces loaves all alike.

The absoluteness of power in creation is manifested from the creation of the first man, Adam, peace be upon him. If the matter of reproduction rests on the existence of a male and a female, from which the bulk of mankind came, then absolute power breaks this rule at every stage of the rational division of it: Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, from neither father nor mother; He created Eve from a father without a mother; and He created Jesus, peace be upon him, from a mother without a father.

Since it is Allah who increases in creation, do not be astonished or disbelieve when you hear the Prophetic hadith: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw Jibril, and he had six hundred wings." Affirm it, for you are not responsible for the how; rather, you are only required to verify the report: whether it came from Allah or did not, whether it is authentically from the Messenger of Allah or not. Be like al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), when they told him about the Isra' and the Mi'raj and said: "Your companion says such and such," and al-Siddiq said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth."

Therefore, those who search into the causes (ilal) of the rulings should leave off searching into them, and it suffices for them to verify their source: if it is from Allah, then it is incumbent upon me to act simply because Allah commanded me, so the cause of the ruling is that Allah commanded it, whether or not I understood its wisdom...

So His saying, "He increases in creation what He wills" [Fatir: 1], is evidence of absolute power that nothing can frustrate...

Then the verse concludes with what reassures hearts regarding this absoluteness: "Indeed Allah is over all things Competent" [Fatir: 1]. This is the reason, meaning: do not be astonished, for it is the power of Allah, which nothing can frustrate. And "shay'" (thing) here encompasses all kinds, for it includes everything from the atom to the galaxy. He, glorified be He, says to a thing "Be," and it is; so it is as though it exists in the realm of the unseen, awaiting the command to appear.

Since He, may He be exalted, is the Creator, creation requires that God provide the created being with what sustains it. First, it needs mercy for the continuation of its life. Therefore He sends down rain, and it brings the earth to life with vegetation, so that a person may plant, eat and drink. This is the foundation of his material life. Then He also provides for the foundation of his spiritual and moral life, sending down what preserves his values and what organizes his life with good conduct toward others. This is the method about which God said:

﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 32].

If God wills mercy for a servant, no one can withhold it from him. "What He opens" means: what He gives and bestows. "There is none to withhold it" means there is no preventer or restrainer of it. "And what He withholds, there is none to release it after Him" means there is no giver of it apart from God.

Consider the Qur'anic style in "what He opens" in contrast with its counterpart. It does not say "what He closes" but says "what He withholds, there is none to release it after Him." Why? The scholars said: because a closed thing may be opened by someone through trickery or force, whereas no one can obtain anything that God has withheld.

Among the meanings of this opening and this mercy is the message which God singled out for our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Therefore the disbelievers said:

﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from one of the two towns?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 31].

And they said: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ [Sad: 8].

God responded to them: ﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world…﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 32].

That is: show good manners toward God. It is He who apportioned for you the affairs of this world and your means of living. Would He leave the distribution of revelation to you and your desires, so that it descends upon whomever you wish?

Opening (fatḥ) is the removal of a barrier between two things. It may be physical, as when we open a door or a suitcase, as in the Qur'an: ﴿When they opened their belongings, they found their merchandise returned to them﴾ [Yusuf: 65].

Opening may also be non-physical, such as opening with goodness, or with mercy, like the revelation which God specially granted to our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Among its uses is His saying:

﴿Do you tell them what God has opened to you?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 76], meaning: from the revelation present in the Torah concerning the description of the Prophet (ﷺ). This is an opening of goodness and blessing in a non-physical sense.

Among the meanings of opening is decision and the resolving of disputes between adversaries, as in His saying:

﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth, for You are the best of deciders﴾ [al-A'raf: 89].

The reason for His saying "What God opens for the people of mercy, none can withhold" is that He, may He be exalted, is one, without partner, and there is no god besides Him. If there were another god with Him, that god would have a different opinion. But God alone acts in His dominion as one who has no partner. Otherwise, how could He be confident that when He says to a thing "Be!" it is, unless the thing obeys Him?

God says this command, and He knows that the thing will obey. No one can say to Him, "Do not obey." Therefore, the first to bear witness to divinity and to the oneness of the One is God Himself, may He be exalted. He bore witness to it for Himself, saying:

﴿God bears witness that there is no god but He﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. This is the witness of the Essence to the Essence. Therefore things responded to Him with "Be," and they were; they heard, obeyed and carried out.

Recite: ﴿When the sky is split open, and it hearkens to its Lord, and it is right that it should﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 1-2], meaning: it heard with awareness, and it is right that it should hear and obey, for it has no other god to oppose it if it obeys.

After the Truth, may He be exalted, bore witness to Himself with the witness of the Essence to the Essence, the angels bore witness to it by way of direct observation. Then those possessed of knowledge bore witness by way of demonstrative proof:

﴿God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those possessed of knowledge…﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18].

Then the verse is concluded with His saying: ﴿He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾. Yes, since He, may He be exalted, is one God without partner, who sends His mercy to whomever He wills and withholds from whomever He wills, He is Mighty. The Mighty is the one who is not overcome and is not resisted. But this might and this dominance do not proceed from brutality, injustice or tyranny; they proceed from wisdom. ﴿He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾. So He, may He be exalted, is wise in His giving and wise in His withholding. And wisdom, as we have said, is placing a thing in its proper place.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 35, verse 3:

God, glorified is He, bestows favour upon His servants and reminds them of His blessings upon them, and He mentions the first of these blessings, which is the blessing of creation from non-existence. God, glorified is He, wished to present this matter to them in a way in which He shares with them in acknowledging it, so the expression did not come in the form of a statement: "I created you." Rather it came in the form of a question so that they themselves would say and affirm: ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾

It is well known that a statement is liable to be denied, whereas a question cannot be denied. You do not ask about something you have done unless you are confident that the answer will come in accordance with your intention. When a person denies your favour, you do not say to him: "I did such-and-such for you," because he may deny you. Rather you say: "Did I not provide such-and-such for you on such-and-such a day?" At that point he cannot do otherwise than acknowledge your favour, for he will find no answer to your question except affirmation.

Likewise, God, glorified is He, establishes His blessings upon them so that the acknowledgment becomes a proof against them, and He asks them, while He, glorified is He, knows best: ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you?﴾ Then God, glorified is He, Himself states the conclusion: ﴿There is no deity but He﴾, and He did not have them say it themselves, because they were (confounded). The logic would have been: since He, glorified is He, is the Creator and the Provider, then it is incumbent upon you to believe in Him. He, glorified is He, said it in the third-person form ﴿There is no deity but He﴾ and did not say "except Me," as if He, glorified is He, were the witness in this matter, as if He were speaking of the unseen.

As for His saying ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾, it means: how, after this, are you diverted from His monotheism and from belief in Him...

This is consolation for our master, the Messenger of Allah, just as his Lord addressed him, saying: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 9]. You are not the first messenger whose people have denied him; those before you were also denied. This is a natural matter, because heaven sends a messenger only when corruption becomes widespread and people lose the inner restraint (al-wazi') and the deterrent (al-radi'), neither from the self toward the self nor from society.

We have said that the Creator, glory be to Him, placed within the human soul a self-deterrent that restrains it when it departs from its Lord's methodology. This is the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwama). If this soul becomes hidden and the soul that commands to evil (al-nafs al-ammara bil-su') prevails over it, the role of society comes, which enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong. If society too becomes corrupt, a new messenger must come with a new miracle to renew for people what they have neglected of God's religion.

That the message of Muhammad is the final one, with no messenger after him, is a testimony for his community that good will always remain among them, and that they will continue to be trusted with the religion of God.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾ [Fatir: 4], it means: in the Hereafter. So whoever among your people denies you, either Allah will seize him in this world as He seized the deniers of the earlier nations, or He will delay his punishment until the Hereafter.

After this, the Truthful, glory be to Him, speaks of the third principle of the sources of legislation (usul al-tashri' - the foundations of divine law). Having spoken of divinity and unity, and having spoken of the Messenger, He now speaks of the third matter about which they differed, which is resurrection, gathering, and reckoning:

﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true, so let not the worldly life deceive you...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 5:

It means: His promise is true, that you will be returned to Allah in the Hereafter, and He will hold you to account and recompense you, the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil. This is a principle well known and practised in all societies, even the primitive ones, and even atheists act upon this principle: He gives the diligent and punishes the negligent. Indeed, some of these people set down laws of reward and punishment that are harsher and more severe than the laws of Allah, such as the laws of execution by hanging and the confiscation of property, and so on.

A society cannot be set right except by this principle. If its application is disturbed, society is corrupted, individuals are discouraged, and chaos spreads. And why not, when the good-doer does not reap the fruit of his goodness and the criminal is not punished for his crime? Therefore, we must cultivate in people the restraint of the desire for good and the fear of evil, so that the good-doer increases in his goodness and the wrongdoer refrains from his evil.

How could this principle not be accepted in a world full of injustices, transgressions, oppression and tyranny, and then the time not come when everyone receives what he deserves?

Therefore I often mention what passed between us and the Communists who deny the matter of resurrection and reckoning. I would say to them: You have seized your enemies and killed them, confiscated their wealth, and done to them terrible things, because in your view they changed the standards of giving. So what of those who did this and committed injustice, yet escaped from you, and your hands did not reach them with punishment?

And what of the oppressors before you and after you? Is it not right to affirm an appointed time that gathers all of them together for reckoning, where each of them receives his recompense? Does this recompense not gladden you and soothe your hearts when you see the oppressor seized for his oppression?

Therefore, you ought to believe in this Day, not deny it and disbelieve in it, for it rests upon the same principle that you yourselves proclaim.

Therefore you notice that the address here is to all people: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾ [Fatir: 5], meaning: His promise of the Resurrection, the Raising and the Reckoning. This is a matter addressed to all people. And the promise of Allah is true, because a promise derives its truthfulness from the one who promises and from his power to fulfil it, and who is more capable than Allah?

It follows, then, that we should trust a promise when it comes from Allah, the Glorified, and not trust the promise of one who has no power in himself.

We have previously explained that a person promises and intends to fulfil at the time of promising, but he does not possess the means of fulfilment; something unforeseen may befall him, or circumstances may change, preventing him from keeping his promise. Therefore our Lord teaches us a lofty etiquette in this matter in Surat al-Kahf, where He says, the Glorified: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," except [when adding], "If Allah wills"﴾ [al-Kahf: 23-24]. Making your action contingent upon the will of your Lord spares you from lying if you fail to fulfil it; you may say: "I intended to fulfil it, but Allah did not will it."

Therefore no promise is described as true except the promise of Allah, because He, the Glorified, alone possesses all the means of fulfilling His promise. Nothing hinders Him from fulfilling it, and no one can prevent Him.

And since the promise of Allah is true, ﴿so let not the worldly life deceive you﴾ [Fatir: 5]: let it not delude you. For people are of various natures: some are deceived by the praise of people for them, and some are deceived in themselves. This is the one whom the worldly life deceives with its desires, so he lives in it without obligations and without commitments, as the disbelievers did when they worshipped stones, because they were gods without obligations.

Therefore our Lord warns us: let not the world deceive you away from something higher than it, which is the Hereafter. And it suffices as a disparagement of this life that Allah the Exalted named it "dunya" (the lower), and the counterpart of the lower is the higher life, which is the Hereafter. The meaning is: let not the world deceive you away from the requirement of Allah, which qualifies you for a higher life.

We have previously explained that, for a human being, the "dunya" is the period of his stay in it, not the whole lifespan of the world. Your life in this world, despite its brevity, is a presumed life, and your bliss in it is in proportion to your activity in it. But your life in the Hereafter is certain, and your bliss there is in proportion to Allah's capacities. And however much of the worldly bliss you attain, what spoils it for you is that it will vanish: either you leave it and die, or it leaves you, and you remain in the world despite your wealth and enjoyment of it, troubled, preoccupied, fearful of losing the blessing. But in the Hereafter the blessing is lasting and enduring, neither cut off nor withheld. Therefore, if you are deceived by the world, make this comparison.

Therefore, when the Truthful, the Glorified, spoke of this life, He described it as "dunya," and when He spoke of the Hereafter He said: ﴿And indeed, the Final Abode is the true life, if they only knew﴾ [al-Ankabut: 64]. The meaning of "al-hayawan" is: the true life that endures, which no death or annihilation threatens. Therefore you must be attentive, and choose the alternative that is more advantageous and more beneficial for you. Thus we say to those who relied upon Allah and lived under the protection of Allah and upon the method of Allah: they have known how to manage their lives, and took them by the shortest routes; and we describe these people as "makr" (cunning), meaning lofty cunning, good cunning.

In another place, the Truthful, the Glorified, shows us the snares of the world and the means of its deception, and says: ﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires: women and children and heaped-up piles of gold and silver and branded horses and cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, but with Allah is the best return﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 14].

His saying, the Glorified: ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾ [Fatir: 5], i.e., Satan. Deception and delusion either come from the soul itself without an external cause, or there is an evil devil who deceives you and whispers to you. Thus you are facing two enemies: either the world with its desires, or Satan with his prodding and his incitement. Our Lord has warned us against him, saying: ﴿And if a prodding from Satan should touch you, seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [al-A'raf: 200].

It means: be alert to this enemy and be wary of him, for his enmity toward you is ancient, since your father Adam, and his hatred for you is clear and open. Therefore you must take a stance toward him. For this reason, the Exalted says after it:

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 6:

As long as he is an enemy to you, openly declaring hostility, it is not permissible for you to make peace with him, to submit to him, or to obey him; for when you obey him, he grows accustomed to his enmity towards you. Therefore, you must oppose him and keep him within his limits. How? The minimum of faith (ضعف الإيمان, ad'af al-iman) is that you do not obey him. If you wish to be stronger than him, then take revenge on him and enrage him by turning toward the opposite of what he demands of you. He commands evil, so you do good; he commands wickedness, so you strive for goodness. It is as though you are mocking him and teaching him a lesson after which he has no choice but to turn away from you, because you have employed his enmity for your own benefit and profited from it, and this is what enrages him.

You may apply this principle with any other enemy, whether he is one of the human devils or one of the jinn devils. You can make his enmity towards you a motive toward goodness and toward loving everything beautiful. The intelligent person is one who benefits from his enemy more than he benefits from his friend...

The true believer can benefit from the enmity of his enemies in many respects. For example, he works and strives to surpass his enemy, rather than being lazy so that he falls behind him in rank and standing; he avoids faults and evil deeds so as not to give his enemy the opportunity to gloat over him... etc.

And if the generous person captivates you with his generosity and you are indebted to him for his kindness, the stingy person has no favour over you, and you are not a captive to him in anything...

The meaning of ﴿فَاتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّا﴾ ("so take him as an enemy") is that you must charge all your energies and all your talents to cultivate in yourself the necessary immunity against his temptations and his whispering of evil to you. If you wish to rise in opposing him, then increase the good deeds that he hates. If he comes to you in prayer to spoil it for you, then enrage him by being humble in it and increasing in its beautification.

﴿إِنَّمَا يَدْعُو حِزْبَهُ لِيَكُونُوا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾ ("He only calls his party so that they will be among the companions of the Blaze") means: he has a party and a group whom he tries to multiply. Therefore, Allah the Exalted said in another place:

﴿اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطَانُ فَأَنسَاهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ أُولَـٰئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطَانِ أَلَا إِنَّ حِزْبَ الشَّيْطَانِ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾ [al-Mujadila: 19].

The meaning of ḥizb (party): a group that is zealously committed to an idea for which they work, in opposition to another group that opposes them, and they too work for an idea that serves them.

The reason he calls his party to be a multitude is so that those who wander in confusion regarding the method of Allah and who deviate from it, in opposition to faith and obedience, will increase in number. This is the reason.

As for His saying ﴿لِيَكُونُوا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾, the lam here is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), and its meaning is: you desire a thing for one reason, but it ends in another reason contrary to your aim.

And His saying ﴿مِنْ أَصْحَابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾ indicates that between them and the Fire there is an affinity, and that it desires them and loves them, until a companionship arises between them.

After Allah, glory be to Him, has mentioned the party of Satan, He pronounces the judgment upon them: ﴿Those who disbelieve, for them is a severe punishment﴾ [Fatir: 7]. And in contrast: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [Fatir: 7]:

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good...?﴾

﴿Is one for whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive, so that he sees it as good...?﴾ This is an interrogative construction (istifham), but its counterpart is not mentioned. Its implied meaning is: "Is he equal to one for whom his evil deed has not been made attractive?"

Allah, glorified is He, does not state the answer because it is known, and no one could say anything other than that they are not equal. Among people are those who commit a sin and know that it is a sin, and they stop at that and do not go beyond it. Others go further: they commit the sin and claim that it is good. This person's calamity is greater, because he committed a transgression when he did the sin, and committed another transgression when he claimed it was good. This is the meaning of ﴿so he saw it as good﴾, and it is a derangement of vision and misguidance.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, says after it: ﴿Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. Many have paused at this verse, saying: "If Allah is the One who guides and the One who misguides, then why is the human being held accountable?" To clarify this matter, we must explain the meaning of guiding (yahdi) and misguiding (yudill). Guiding means: He points him to the path of good and directs him to it. This guidance from Allah is for all people. Whoever hears this guidance and walks by its light reaches the path of good, and so he receives from Allah assistance and an increase in guidance, as He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And those who accept guidance — He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17].

As for one who shuts his hearing, does not listen, and is not guided, he loses the path and deviates from the right way. Allah then also assists him toward his aim, increases him in misguidance, and seals his heart so that what he wants is what he gets: no faith enters his heart and no disbelief leaves it. About such people Allah says:

﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease, and for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10].

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, says about the people of Thamud: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17]. The meaning of ﴿We guided them﴾ is: We indicated to them and directed them to the path of good, but they rejected this indication and opposed Allah, so they went astray, and Allah left them in their misguidance. That is, He increased them in misguidance.

We had already clarified this issue earlier and said: Suppose you want to go to a certain place, and you stand at a junction of roads not knowing which one will lead you to your goal. So you go to a traffic policeman and ask him where the road is, and he directs you to it. You thank him and acknowledge his kindness. When he sees you obedient to him and grateful for his favor, he says to you: "But ahead on this road there is an obstacle, and I will walk with you until you pass it." In this way Allah, glorified is He, treats those who are guided:

﴿And those who accept guidance — He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17].

Allah, glorified is He, addressed His Prophet (ﷺ) saying:

﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas: 56], and He addressed him saying: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. Thus He affirmed for the Prophet (ﷺ) guidance in the sense of direction and indication, but He negated for him guidance in the sense of granting the ability to be guided; the one who grants that is Allah.

Then Allah, glorified is He, did not leave this matter as it is. Rather, He explained whom He guides and whom He misguides, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67], and He said: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [al-Saff: 5]. What guidance can there be for a human being after he has disbelieved in Allah, deviated from His way, corrupted the land, and wronged the servants?

As for His saying, ﴿So let not your soul go out in grief over them﴾, the meaning is: Do not destroy yourself with grief over their not believing. Allah explained this meaning in His saying:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 6].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was keen on the guidance of his people, and he suffered greatly when any one of them strayed from the path of faith. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said about His Prophet Muhammad: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; he is anxious over you, and to the believers kind and merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128].

Then Allah, glorified is He, consoles His Messenger (ﷺ), saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾. That is: nothing hidden of their actions is concealed from Him, and He will requite them with the punishment they deserve in proportion to the aversion that proceeded from them. So be reassured and do not grieve.

Meaning of "yursil al-riyah" (He sends the winds): He sets them in motion. By the movement of the winds the full benefit of existence is secured. Do you not see that when the wind is still, a person feels constricted and tries to move it himself, with his hand or with a fan, for example? This is because your breathing is not complete except through the movement of air and the exchange of carbon dioxide for oxygen, and this process is not completed except by moving the air. Hence they say: "If the air does not pass over you, then you pass over it," meaning: move it yourself.

As a result of the movement of the winds, the clouds are stirred up, ﴿so they raise clouds﴾ [Fatir: 9], meaning: they agitate them and move them from their places, so that after they gather they go to where God wills the rain to fall. Thus the movement of the clouds is not self-generated, but follows the movement of the winds. This matter helps us understand the words of the Most High: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they pass away as the passing of clouds﴾ [An-Naml: 88].

So the mountains, which we suppose to be stationary, are in reality passing and moving like the movement of the clouds. Just as the clouds do not pass by themselves, but by the movement of the winds, so the mountains do not pass by themselves, but by the movement of the earth, and the mountains are fixed upon the earth like pegs; therefore they move with its movement: ﴿The handiwork of God, who has perfected everything. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do﴾ [An-Naml: 88].

Some did not perceive the movement of the earth which the movement of the mountains follows, so they said regarding His words ﴿and they pass as the passing of clouds﴾ [An-Naml: 88] that this refers to the Hereafter. But where are the mountains in the Hereafter, when God says of them: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up﴾ [Al-Ma'arij: 9]? Then, how would God bestow favour upon them and argue by the wondrous workmanship of His movement of the mountains in the Hereafter, where there is no obligation and no place for softening hearts and inclining them toward faith?

This concerns the movement of the winds. As for their stillness, He the Most High says: ﴿If He wills, He stills the wind so they become motionless upon its surface﴾ [Ash-Shura: 33], and what is meant is the ships that the winds propel. If you say: does this verse retain this meaning after the development that has come upon ships, and after the sails have vanished and been replaced by machines that move ships without need for the movement of air?

We say: Yes, the verse will continue to bear this meaning for as long as God wills, because modern inventions have not taken their Creator by surprise. And who said that "rih" (wind) is air? "Rih" is strength, whatever it may be. Consider His words: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you falter and your strength (rih) depart﴾ [Al-Anfal: 46], meaning: your strength, whatever it is, whether the strength of air, or the strength of electricity, or the strength of steam and engines, etc.

We note in the style of this verse that the verb ﴿arsala﴾ [Fatir: 9] comes in the past tense, but (tuthir) in the present tense. He, glory be to Him, did not say "fa-atharat sahaban" (and they raised clouds); He said "arsala" (He sent), meaning He commanded that they be sent. This is a matter that has ended and been completed. But the raising and moving of the clouds is a continually renewed matter at every moment, so the present tense, which denotes the present and the future, suits it.

Or: the meaning ﴿And God is He who sends the winds, so they raise clouds﴾ [Fatir: 9] is in the past tense because the discourse concerns the unseen, and the apparent noun is unseen, namely the Name of Majesty (Allah). Then it shifts from the unseen in ﴿sends the winds﴾ [Fatir: 9] to the first-person speaker, saying ﴿so We drove it﴾ [Fatir: 9], as if God, through the blessing, draws your attention to the unseen which is God the Most High. When you recall that it is God who did this, you become worthy of God addressing you directly.

An example of this is what we said in Surat al-Fatiha: ﴿In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds. The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Sovereign of the Day of Judgement﴾ [Al-Fatiha: 1-4]. All of this is unseen, up to ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [Al-Fatiha: 5].

He did not say "iyyahu na'budu" (Him we worship) to move you from the unseen to direct address with Him, the Glorified; because you have become worthy to address Him and to be addressed by Him, after you have believed in the initial grounds in ﴿All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds. The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Sovereign of the Day of Judgement﴾ [Al-Fatiha: 2-4].

As for the meaning of ﴿So We drove it to a dead land﴾ [Fatir: 9], it means: We drove the clouds, or We drove the water after its descent into channels and rivers, to land in which there is no vegetation and which can benefit from it. This is more indicative of God's power. Consider, for example, the water of the Nile which irrigates Sudan and Egypt: where does it descend? This is evidence that your provision will reach you no matter how far its source is from you.

When the water settles in the earth, the result is ﴿and We revived thereby the earth after its death﴾ [Fatir: 9], meaning: We revived it with vegetation. Then the Truth, glory be to Him, makes the blessings of reviving dead land a proof of another blessing that follows in the Hereafter, so He says: ﴿Thus will be the resurrection﴾ [Fatir: 9], meaning: the resurrection on the Day of Judgement and the revival of the dead from their graves.

So take from what you witness of the revival of the earth a proof of the truth of what is hidden from you. Just as water descends upon dead earth and revives it, so when the spirit descends upon the matter of man buried in the earth, resurrection and rising occur for it, and life stirs within it.

We have previously explained that when scholars analysed the human body, they found it composed of sixteen elements. The first of them is oxygen, and the last is manganese. These are the very elements of the soil in which plants grow.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Whoever desires honour—then to God belongs all honour, entirely...﴾.

The rejection of the messages is a rejection of being a believer who is given duties, following another's opinion and submitting to his command. The Messenger came only to tell us, "Do this" and "Do not do that." Some people see in this obedience a blow to their dignity and honour. They want to be the highest, the one whom no one commands or forbids. Those whom the verse speaks of want honour to be in their own souls.

Here the Exalted corrects their understanding of honour and exposes their foolishness. He says: ﴿Whoever desires honour, then all honour belongs to Allah﴾. That is, true honour, not the claimed kind. True honour is not to be overcome or subdued by anyone, and this honour exists only in the presence of Allah. However far a person reaches in worldly strength and tyranny, he will inevitably be overcome, and death will inevitably subdue him. If you are enamoured of an honour that does not pass away, it is found only with Allah.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, teaches us wisdom, saying: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die﴾ (al-Furqan: 58). This means: I know you and I know your weakness, and that you need someone to rely upon to accomplish for you the matters beyond your capacity. So beware of turning to other than Me, for I am the Everlasting who does not die. If you rely upon a weak one like yourself, he may die before he fulfils your need. Likewise, whoever desires honour should be in the embrace of Allah, taking honour from His honour and strength from His strength. Whoever is in the embrace of Allah, Allah bestows upon him some of His attributes and pours them upon him.

Likewise, our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), gives us this lesson. He was in the cave with al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), and al-Siddiq said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looked down at his feet, he would see us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), certain in his Lord, said: "O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is Allah?" The Qur'an has recorded his words: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ (al-Tawbah: 40).

This tranquillity that filled the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) originates in Allah's companionship with him and his companion. This companionship requires that Allah bestow upon both of them some of His attributes, the Exalted. If He, the Exalted, cannot be seen, then whoever is in His company likewise cannot be seen.

The phrase ﴿all honour﴾ (al-'izzah jami'an) means: all kinds of honour...

Then the Exalted says: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾. We address Allah in terms of height, although He, the Exalted, is in every place and has no place...

The meaning of ﴿the good word﴾ (al-kalim al-tayyib) is a general description of every speech that points to the path of good. The Qur'an has given us an example of this in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents a parable: a good word is like a good tree, its root firmly fixed and its branches in the sky, giving its produce every season by the permission of its Lord﴾ (Ibrahim: 24-25).

The scholars have attempted to define this word. They said it is: "There is no god but Allah," "Glory be to Allah," "Praise be to Allah," and "There is no power nor strength except with Allah." But this definition narrows the broad meaning that Allah intended for it. The more correct statement is that the good word is every speech that leads to good.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and righteous deed raises it﴾. After speaking of the ascent of the good word, He speaks of the elevation of righteous deed, because a person may utter a good word without it achieving its purpose and without translating it into action. He may say it perhaps out of hypocrisy, like those who said "There is no god but Allah" hypocritically, to flee from being killed. Yet it still ascends to Allah. Allah says: protect him by this word in his worldly life, and do not harm him so long as he has uttered it. But he has no reward for it in the Hereafter, because reward comes from the deed that serves the meaning of the word. So the consideration is in the deed, and righteous deed is what is raised to Allah. It protects you in this world and protects you in the Hereafter, and gathers for you both goods.

Then the Exalted mentions the opposite: ﴿And those who plot evil deeds, for them is severe punishment, and the plotting of those will perish﴾. The verb makr (plotting) takes a prepositional complement; one says makara bi-fulan (he deceived someone), and makara-hu (he deceived him) means he tricked him. It also takes a direct object, as in yamkurun al-sayyi'at, whose original form is yamkurun al-makrat al-sayyi'at ("they plot the evil plots"), where the adjective describes a verbal noun derived from the verb's root, as in ﴿those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾ (al-Nisa': 122), meaning righteous deeds. Alternatively, makara can be taken as "he plotted a plot," so the meaning is: "those who committed evil deeds."

Then the Exalted explains the recompense for evil plotting: ﴿for them is severe punishment﴾. Why? Because when you plot, you are as if you want to steal something from Allah, and you think He will not know of you, forgetting that you are devising the plot in secret, while He knows the secret and the private conversation. When you plot and when you devise, you devise according to your capacity, and your Lord, mighty and majestic, likewise plots and devises according to His capacity. His power, the Exalted: ﴿And they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ (al-Anfal: 30). Therefore this plotting ends in loss and ruin, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and the plotting of those will perish﴾. It is a plot that perishes, like barren land that produces nothing and bears no fruit. From this is His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude and settled their people in the house of ruin?﴾ (Ibrahim: 28).

This plotting, which its doer thought would benefit him, raise him over his adversary, and make himself superior to him, perishes, and does not bear its fruit. Would that it perished and the matter ended there! Instead, it turns against him and draws severe punishment upon its doer.

The meaning of ﴿for them is severe punishment﴾: the lam (la-hum) denotes possession. Thus the sense is inverted: they are deserving of punishment, as if the punishment is eager for them, just as a person is eager for what he owns. It is a punishment that is attached to them and never leaves them.

The verse addresses the first creation of man, the vicegerent (khalifah). This creation had stages. The first man, Adam (peace be upon him), was created in an initial form from the substance of the earth, which is dust mixed with water until it became clay (ṭīn). This clay passed through several states. If you leave the clay until it putrefies and gives off an odour, it becomes *ḥama' masnūn* (putrid, black moulded clay). If you leave it until it dries and hardens, it becomes *ṣalṣāl* (dry clay that rings when struck). These are therefore stages of one substance, from which God formed Adam. Then He breathed into him of His spirit. This is the first creation, from which He took Eve, and from the two of them procreation and offspring proceed.

Before the Exalted speaks of the creation of man, He speaks of what He created for man before he came into existence. He spoke of the creation of the heavens and the earth: ﴿All praise is due to God, Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ [Fāṭir: 1]. Then He spoke of the angels who bring revelation to the messengers from among mankind. Then He sent down water from the sky by which the earth brings forth growth.

All of these are the means of sustaining human life, which God brought into being before He brought man into being. He guaranteed for him the means of his life, both material and spiritual. The material means are sustenance: food, drink and air. The spiritual means are the method and the Qur'an. For this reason He said: ﴿The Most Merciful. He taught the Qur'an. He created man﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 1–3].

Man was created for a purpose, like a craftsman who determines the purpose of the thing he makes before he begins it. We have said: the one who made the television or the refrigerator did not make it and then say, "Look at what this machine is used for." Rather, he determined its purpose and defined its goal before making it. Likewise, before the Exalted created man, He determined his movement in life and what would make him happy in it. He laid down for him the method of the Qur'an before he was created. Then the creation of the substance came after the laying down of the method.

When the Exalted speaks of the creation of man, He says: ﴿And God created you from dust﴾ [Fāṭir: 11]. The style is as though He is speaking of an absent one, and He did not say, "I created you." It is as though we say, "God created man from dust." This is because the means of address between a speaker and an addressee come in three forms: the first person pronoun "I", the second person "you", or the third person "he".

When the speaker speaks, he says, "I did it." It is possible that he is lying. If he is addressed, "You did it," it is possible that he is flattering. But when the style is in the third person, "He did it," then we are clear of the claim in the speaker and of hypocrisy in the addressee.

When we say "He created," it means that there is none other than Him. We have already said that the third person pronoun "He" refers only to the Exalted and Glorified.

If you survey the verses of creation in the Qur'an, you will find them in the third-person style in one hundred and seven verses, beginning with His saying in Sūrat al-Baqarah: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29], and ending with the Sūrat al-Falaq: ﴿Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, from the evil of what He created﴾ [al-Falaq: 1–2]. In the first-person style they are in seventy-six verses, such as: ﴿…Indeed, We created you from male and female…﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 13].

In the second-person style they are in four places: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 191].

And His saying: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [al-A'rāf: 12].

And His saying: ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ [al-Isrā': 61].

The third-person style is the most common of these styles, because speaking of an absent one is free of claim and free of the hypocrisy of direct address.

But what is the meaning of *khalq* (creation)? The scholars said: *khalq* is bringing into being from non-existence for a wisdom or a prior purpose, not merely bringing into being from non-existence. How? If you take a large piece of dry clay and throw it on the ground, it will break into pieces of various shapes. Perhaps you will find among them one in the shape of a crescent, another in the shape of a star, and another in the shape of a human or animal face. This is called bringing into being, but it is not called creation, because creation is purposeful bringing into being for a determined end and a desired wisdom. This is the task of the Creator alone, glory be to Him.

If you say: how, when God affirms for us a creation in His saying: ﴿So blessed is God, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minūn: 14]?

We say: the Creator, glory be to Him, values the efforts of human beings and does not deprive them of their rights. For this reason He affirms for them a share in creation, with the clear difference between God's creation and the creation of others. When man is described as a creator, God is the best of creators, because He creates from non-existence, while you create from what exists. Your creation remains in one state and stagnates upon it, whereas God's creation develops, life stirs in it, and it is nourished, grows and reproduces, and so on.

We illustrated this with the glassmaker, who takes sand, which was created by God, then treats it in a certain manner and transforms it into glass. Yes, you have created something, because this cup did not exist before, and you brought it into being. But it is from an existing substance created by God, and the mind that thought of it is one of God's creatures, and the fire that melted it is from God's creation.

Then, you cannot give this cup the attribute of life, so that it grows or reproduces. Therefore, if God affirms a creation for you, He, glory be to Him, is the best of creators.

The Exalted says here: ﴿And God created you from dust﴾ [Fāṭir: 11], and in other places He said: ﴿from clay﴾ [al-An'ām: 2], and He said ﴿from black moulded clay﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 26], and He said: ﴿from clay like pottery﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 14]. There is no contradiction between these statements, because they are stages of one substance, as we have explained. It is like the garment you wear: you say, this garment is of cotton, or of yarn, or of woven fabric. These are stages through which one substance passes.

There is no contradiction in the stages. The contradiction would be if a thing were one rank and then you made it into several ranks. Rather, this matter is stages of a single rank, like the child who becomes a boy, then a youth, then a man, then an elderly man, and so on. All these are stages of one person.

The Exalted has decided in His creation about certain things and has forbidden the intellect to think about certain things. He said: I created for you the universe and the substance, and I guaranteed for you the means of your life. If you wish to elevate yourself, then employ your intellect in the substance created by God, and draw conclusions from it according to your capacity. But do not occupy your mind with two matters in which thinking is of no benefit. These two matters are the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the creation of people, because God says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor of their own selves, nor was I one to take misleading ones as helpers﴾ [al-Kahf: 51].

The creation of the heavens and the earth and the creation of man is a matter that none of you witnessed, and there was no helper with God, glory be to Him, to inform you of what happened. But beware: there will come in the future misleaders who will mislead you about this matter, saying to you, as the misleaders say now, that the heavens and the earth were one molten piece, and such and such happened to it, or that the first origin of man was an ape that evolved into a human. Beware of these people, and take your knowledge only from the One who witnessed it and knows it, who is God, the Exalted.

But God created the intellect as an instrument for thinking, and made for it channels through which it reaches the truth, and inferring from what it has seen to what is hidden from it. So the intellect must reflect on what it sees and infer from it what it does not see.

We did not witness the process of creation, but we did witness the process of death, and death is the undoing of creation, just as demolition is the undoing of construction.

This is a philosophical matter in which the intellect has a role. If you want to build a ten-storey building, for example, you begin by building the first floor. But if you want to demolish it, you begin with the tenth floor. Demolition is the reverse of construction. Likewise, death is the opposite of life.

What we have not witnessed of the process of creation, God has informed us of in His Book. He said: I created you from dust that became clay, then the clay became black moulded clay, and the black moulded clay became dry clay like pottery, shaped in the form of a human, then God breathed the spirit into it, and life stirred in it.

We have witnessed death and seen it come as the reverse of the process of creation. The first thing in death is that the spirit departs from the body, and it hardens until it becomes like pottery, then it decomposes, and its smell changes as though it were black moulded clay. Then the earth absorbs what moisture is in it, so that it returns to dust and crumbled matter mixed with the dust of the earth, and returns to its mother from which it came.

So take from what you have witnessed as evidence for the truth of what God has informed you of that you have not witnessed.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of creation, He spoke of two stages. The first: the creation of the first man, Adam (peace be upon him), from clay. And in order for reproduction to take place for the building of the earth, the second stage was that He created his spouse for him. He said: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate…﴾ [al-A'rāf: 189].

The matter allows room for speculation. It is valid that He took a piece from Adam and created Eve from it. It is also valid that this piece was itself from clay. But He was content with the first formation of the man. From Adam and Eve He produced offspring, and the vicegerency on earth was fulfilled.

To come out of the maze in this matter, we say: His saying ﴿and from it He created its mate﴾ [al-Nisā': 1] means: from its kind, from the kind of its creation, as He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128], meaning: from your kind.

But would God create this creation and appoint His vicegerent on earth, and then leave him without supplying him with the method that governs the movement of his life? No. He must send down for him the method, because the meaning of vicegerency requires that this method exist.

When the Exalted gives His vicegerent dominion over things that obey his command, that dominion may deceive him. So He says to him: remember that you are not original, and that you are a vicegerent. As long as you remember that you are a vicegerent, you will not transgress. What makes you transgress is that you think you are original in the universe. The original one in the universe is the one who preserves what has been bestowed upon him, who does not fall ill and does not die, and with whom there is none stronger than him. So remember that you are appointed, and as long as you are appointed, you must carry out the commands of the One who appointed you.

After the Exalted spoke of the first creation from dust and the creation of the wife, He tells us of the general creation from which all human beings come after Adam and Eve. Through marriage, creation comes about through the drop of semen. So He says: ﴿Then from a drop of semen, then He made you into pairs﴾ [Fāṭir: 11].

In another place He detailed the stages of the drop of semen, saying: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 5].

The first marriage among the children of Adam took place by distancing: a man of this lineage would marry his sister from another lineage, and so the distancing was according to the increase of offspring, as far as possible. And the matter of this distancing is what led to the first murder in humanity, the matter of Qābīl and Hābīl. When the world expanded and people multiplied, marriage to a sister, a maternal aunt or a paternal aunt was forbidden.

Science has also established the importance of distance in marriage, and that marriage between close relatives produces weaker offspring than marriage with distant ones. Even in agriculture they have proven that sowing grain harvested from the same soil gives a smaller yield, so in farming they resorted to cross-breeding.

The Prophet (ﷺ) urged this distance, saying: [hadith text as given in the commentary]. That is: do not marry someone who is closely related to you, because close relatives share the same characteristics and the same blood. But in outside marriage, the characteristics are different and the blood is different, so the offspring come out stronger.

For this reason the Arab poet noticed this matter, and said:

Let him be warned, whoever has a distant concern: marrying the children of paternal aunts.
He is not safe from weakness and sickness, though you feed him, he does not thrive.

They have observed the weakness of offspring in families whose children marry their relatives, and they praised estrangement. A poet said:

A youth whose mother was not a near paternal cousin, he grows weak, and the offspring of close relatives may well grow weak.

And another, who distances himself from his paternal cousin in marriage despite loving her, says:

I passed over the paternal cousin, though she was beloved, fearing that her offspring would weaken me.

Then He says, may He be exalted: ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾ [Fāṭir: 11]. The process of a female's conception takes place as a result of the meeting of male and female under the canopy of the law and the method of God. Scholars have spoken at length about the matter of a woman's pregnancy: is she the one responsible for it, or the man? Finally, we have heard from the analyses they have carried out that the man is responsible for the sperm that determines male or female, while the woman carries the egg that receives this or that.

It is remarkable that the ancient Arab woman noticed the results of modern science, and that she had awareness and understanding of this matter. The Bedouin woman who gave birth only to daughters was angered by her husband, who went and married another woman so she could bear him a son, and he abandoned the first. So she recited verses and said:

Why does Abu Ḥamza not come to us, angry that we do not bear sons?
By God, that is not in our hands; we are like the earth to those who plant in it.
We give them what we were given.

It is remarkable that a Bedouin woman should speak of what modern science reached in the twentieth century. It is as though the Exalted wants to show us that sound natural disposition, far from desire, can reach the realities of the universe. Sound judgment does not combine with the desires of the soul. For this reason they said: the bane of judgment is desire. And from this is what is narrated about our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Qur'an used to descend in accordance with what he thought, and that was only because of the soundness of his natural disposition.

His saying ﴿and gives birth only with His knowledge﴾ [Fāṭir: 11] refers to stages the woman passes through: first she marries, then she conceives, then she gives birth to her child. All these are stages of safety. The Exalted did not mention what may befall the pregnancy of defect: a mother may conceive and her fetus may be miscarried, so she does not give birth.

The miracle accompanying the process of pregnancy is that the blood which flows from a woman during her menstrual cycle turns, when she conceives, into nourishment for the fetus. It is as though this blood is not her provision but the provision of her child, if pregnancy is decreed for her. If pregnancy is not decreed for her, the blood leaves her without her benefiting from it at all.

It is remarkable that this blood suffices for one fetus, and for two or three, and even more. Recently we heard of a woman who gave birth to seven, and yet she was in good health, meaning her weight did not decrease at all. It is as though the Mighty and Majestic Creator reminds us: before you bear the concern of sustenance and provisions, look at what God did for you while you were in your mothers' wombs. For each of you there is a provision from which he will not escape and which will not miss him.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) spoke truly: [hadith text as given in the commentary]. Even with the advance of science now, they have not been able to determine the date of birth with certainty, and this moment will remain in the knowledge of God: ﴿And no female gives birth except with His knowledge﴾ [Fāṭir: 11]. Why? Because we know the duration of pregnancy, but we do not know precisely when the zygote (*al-zīgūt*) attached itself to the womb. For this reason, obstetricians often say that the pregnant woman will give birth within such-and-such a number of days.

So the moment of birth is much like the moment of death in its hiddenness: no one knows it except God. And "knows it" means He knows it with all the circumstances and events surrounding it.

After the woman has delivered her child, she becomes a nurse and a nurturer. The Creator, glory be to Him, then provides the provision of her child so that she can nurse him without taking anything from her own provision, because God's provision to her is continuous, and a thing diminishes if something is taken from it without replenishment.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And no one is granted a long life, nor is a part of his life shortened, except that it is in a Book﴾ [Fatir: 11]. "Yu'ammar" means: God extends his life. In the language there are verbs that are invariably used in the passive form. For example, we say: "zukima fulan" (so-and-so caught a cold), because he did not bring the cold upon himself. Likewise we say: "fa-la 'ummira" (he was granted a long life). He did not grant himself long life; rather, God granted it to him. Therefore it comes in the form of the passive participle, "mu'ammar," and "al-mu'ammar" means: one of long life.

This is one of the points on which the orientalists paused with objections, as usual, because of their ignorance of the Arabic language and its styles. They said: how can one be granted life, so that he lives a hundred years, for example, and then his life is shortened? We say: they are excused, because they do not know that in the language there is a pronoun and a referent for the pronoun.

For example, you say: "I met so-and-so and honoured him," so the "hu" in "akramtuhu" refers back to this so-and-so. And you say: "I gave a dirham in charity and its half" (tasaddaqtu bi-dirhamin wa nisfihi). Does this mean that you gave a dirham in charity, then you returned to it again and halved it? No. The meaning is: I gave a dirham in charity and half a dirham like it. So at one time the pronoun refers to one and the same thing, and at another time it refers to one of its kind, as in: "tasaddaqtu bi-dirhamin wa nisfihi."

A human being has an essence and has attributes. His essence is the substance of his constitution, and his attributes are the qualities that come upon the essence. His being long-lived means that he has reached a great age. Just as the pronoun may refer to something like the first, or to part of its like, so it may refer to part of its essence. The one granted long life is an essence to which long life has been ascribed. So to what does the pronoun in ﴿and no part of his life is shortened﴾ [Fatir: 11] refer? It is correct: when he reaches a hundred years, we cannot cause him to die at the age of twenty, for example.

Therefore: refer the pronoun to the essence, not to the attribute. What is granted long life is granted it, and nothing is taken from his essence. The essence was not ascribed long life except by God's permission, and so the meaning becomes like: "tasaddaqtu bi-dirhamin wa nisfihi."

God Almighty has told us about granting long life when He spoke of the Jews: ﴿And they said: None will enter the Garden except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111].
And they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80].
God replied to them: if you have guaranteed Paradise for yourselves, and that no one can take it from you, then wish for death, which will bring you to it: ﴿Say: If the abode of the Hereafter with God is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 94].
Then God passed judgment upon them: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forth; and God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. And you will surely find them the most eager of people for life, and of those who associated others with God. One of them wishes he could be granted a thousand years, but that being granted long life would not remove him from the punishment; and God is Seeing of what they do﴾ [al-Baqarah: 95-96].

So the meaning of ﴿and no part of his life is shortened﴾ [Fatir: 11] is: from the life of an essence to which long life was ascribed only by God's permission.

As for His saying ﴿except that it is in a Book﴾ [Fatir: 11], that is: in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Everything that happens to lifespans, and in periods of pregnancy and delivery, whether shortening or lengthening, is all inscribed and known in the Preserved Tablet. ﴿Indeed, that is easy for God﴾ [Fatir: 11]: if it is difficult for you and your understanding, it is easy and simple for God, glorified is He.

Consider our master Zakariyya, peace be upon him, when he prayed to God to grant him a righteous son who would inherit prophethood after him, even though he had reached extreme old age and his wife was barren. What offspring after this age, especially if the wife is barren? But if it is by the laws of God, then the matter is easy and facile.

Read: ﴿And indeed I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit from me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub, and make him, my Lord, pleasing. O Zakariyya, We give you good news of a boy whose name is Yahya; We have not given this name to anyone before. He said: My Lord, how can I have a boy, when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age? He said: So it is; your Lord says: it is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing﴾ [Maryam: 5-9].

So: do not measure the matter by your own power and your own laws, because the act is attributed to God, not to a human being.

Likewise our master Musa, peace be upon him: when Pharaoh followed him with his armies until he surrounded him and pressed him hard, Musa's followers said: ﴿Indeed we are overtaken﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 61]. Why not, when the sea was before them and Pharaoh's armies behind them? Musa said, speaking as one who trusts in his Lord and His unbounded power: ﴿By no means!﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 62], that is: they will not overtake us. He said it out of the store of trust he had in God: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 62]. Relief came to him immediately: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff; and it parted, and each part was like a mighty mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 63].

Musa saw a dry path cleaving the sea, so he and his people crossed until they were on the far side. Then he wanted to strike the sea again so that it would return to its flowing state and Pharaoh could not cross it, but his Lord forbade him. The miracle had not ended; it still had a remainder, and God is able to save and destroy by one and the same thing. The dry path remained dry until Pharaoh was deceived by it and crossed to catch up with Musa. When the last of Pharaoh's soldiers had come down, God closed the water over them and returned it to its flow, drowning Pharaoh and his armies. This is the all-encompassing power that no limits confine and that is not subject to causes.

Likewise, consider the matter of creation and procreation: you will find that most people came from a male and a female, and this is the rule. But God's power is not unable to bring creation at every stage of the rational, logical division in this matter. The Creator, glorified is He, created Adam without father or mother, then created Eve from a father without a mother, and created Jesus from a mother without a father. So we say: the matter is easy and simple for God, even if you think it difficult.

Then the Almighty says:
﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet, palatable, pleasant to drink, and that one is salty and bitter...﴾

The Truth, glory be to Him, wishes to bring the rational, value-based matter close to us, so He presents it to us in a visible, sensory form: ﴿And the two seas are not alike﴾. It is as if God is saying to us: just as there are sensory things that are not alike in the senses, so too in values there are things that are not alike.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 13:

It is true that night and day are equal at certain times, but the night lengthens in winter and so takes a portion of the day, and the day lengthens in summer and so takes a portion of the night. Therefore the lengthening of one of them is a shortening of the other. This is the meaning of ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾ [Fatir: 13], i.e., He makes this enter into that.

The phenomenon of the night entering into the day and the day entering into the night arises from the inclination of the axis. Just as Allah, glory be to Him, distributed water and preserved it in the vast sea, so too He distributed heat. Were it not for the inclined axis, the side facing the sun would burn and the other side would freeze.

Among the wonders of creation is that a human being who lives at the North Pole or the South Pole has a body temperature of 37, the same as one who lives at the equator, because the human body is built on a special engineering that preserves its appropriate temperature whatever the surroundings, and indeed preserves for each organ within it the temperature suited to it, even though all the organs are in one body, and heat radiates and spreads throughout the whole place.

It is remarkable that the liver, for example, performs its natural function only at a temperature of 40, while the eye's temperature does not exceed 37. So who prevents the heat of the liver from spreading through the whole body and reaching the eye, for example? It is the Creator: ﴿Who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided﴾ [al-A'la: 2-3].

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon﴾ [Fatir: 13], it means He made them submissive to man and placed them at his service, without any power of his over them and without any will of his. The sun and the moon are two signs in the general structure of the universe in which man has no part. Had he had a part in them, their affair would have been corrupted and would not have been upright. Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted...﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 71].

If you say: the corruption of the earth by man is possible, so how could he corrupt the heavens? They say: Did not a people wish that the sky would fall upon them, and they said: ﴿Or You cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾ [al-Isra': 92]? So if the truth had followed the desires of these people, the world would have been ruined.

This is a question that the philosophical school in Germany discussed against another school, and the two held contradictory opinions while living in the same age, and each of them takes its opinion as proof of atheism and of the claim that there is no God. This is remarkable.

One of them says: there is no anomaly in the world; it proceeds according to straight laws, very much like (mechanics), and if this universe had a creating God, creation would vary and anomaly would occur in it.

The other says: the universe does not proceed on a fixed system; rather anomaly occurs in creation, as evidenced by the fact that some are born, for example, disabled; and if the world had a creating God, creation would come out uniform and without difference.

Glory be to God! They want atheism in any way whatsoever; their temperament is to be atheists.

We say to these: Come, let us bring you back to the right and to a common word. O you who want the anomaly of things as proof of the existence of a powerful God, the proof exists; and O you who want the stability of things as proof of the existence of a wise God, the proof exists. But the direction is separate. How?

The fixed system without any anomaly exists in the upper cosmos, which proceeds with regularity and order that does not deviate. The movement of the sun, the moon, the planets and the spheres all proceed on one system that never falters. And now we have been able, for example, to determine the exact moment of an eclipse, and we indeed observe it at precisely its time.

So: if you want stability as proof, take it from the higher spheres, because they must be built upon a fixed system without any anomaly, or else the whole universe would be disordered.

If you want anomaly, observe it in particulars, because the anomaly of particulars does not affect the general order of the universe. Therefore you see: this one is sound, this one is blind, this one is one-eyed, etc. So stability is in its place for a wisdom, and anomaly is in its place for a wisdom, and this and that are two proofs of the existence of the Creating, Powerful God.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿each runs to a term appointed﴾ [Fatir: 13], i.e., each of the sun and the moon runs toward a known time at which their passing away and end will be complete. ﴿That is﴾ [Fatir: 13], i.e., the One who did this and determined it, ﴿Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion﴾ [Fatir: 13], i.e., the perceptible world visible to you. As for the dominion of Allah that you do not see, it is the world of the malakut, which is what is hidden from you and that your senses do not perceive.

Therefore, when our master Ibrahim succeeded in the trial, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124], Allah gave him a great station and made him aware of the malakut that was hidden from others. He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And thus did We show Ibrahim the malakut of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 75]. What follows in the world of the visible dominion that we see arises from the world of the malakut that we do not perceive.

And the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, points to this world, the world of the malakut, in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you criterion [furqan]﴾ [al-Anfal: 29].

How so, when we have not feared Allah except through the furqan, i.e., the Qur'an? What then is the meaning of ﴿He will grant you furqan﴾ [al-Anfal: 29]? They said: the furqan here is that Allah shows you the malakut of the heavens and the earth.

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him do not possess even a qitmir﴾ [Fatir: 13], it means: if the true God created for you such and such, and subjected the sun and the moon to you, then your supposed and imagined gods ﴿do not possess even a qitmir﴾ [Fatir: 13]. So what is the qitmir?

One who reflects on the Noble Qur'an finds that it gives great attention to the date palm. The first to be addressed were the Arabs, and they were the first to be confronted with Islam and invited to it, so the Qur'an addressed them in a way suited to them and mentioned to them examples from their environment. The date palm is well known in the Arab environment, and it has a station in our religion, to the extent that it is attributed to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said, "Honour your aunt, the palm tree."

Although this saying is not authentically established from the Messenger of Allah, what he said was not said from nothing, and this saying must have a basis, and there must be a connection between the human being and the palm tree.

And it is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said to his companions: When Abdullah ibn Umar heard this, he said to his father: It occurred to my mind that it is the palm tree, because its leaves do not fall, and it is more like the believer; everything in it is beneficial. Then Umar went early to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, my son Abdullah said about the tree you mentioned that it is the palm tree. He said: He is right. Umar said: By Allah, I would not be pleased that I had red camels in exchange for it, meaning he was happy that his son understood the statement of the Messenger of Allah.

Scholars have tried to bring this truth closer to minds and to establish the kinship between the human being and the palm tree, and that it may perhaps have been created from the remainder of the clay of our master Adam. They said: the smell of the palm's pollen spathe by which pollination is accomplished is the same as the smell of human semen, and this strengthens the truth of the one who said that it is our aunt.

In the creation of the palm tree in this form there are wonders and secrets, and it is enough that everything in it is beneficial, and nothing of it is discarded. Allah has made it a place of parable and lesson. When He spoke to the Arabs about the crescent, He said: ﴿And the moon, We have determined for it phases until it returns like the old dried palm stalk﴾ [Ya-Sin: 39].

The 'urjun is the stalk that carries the dates when it dries, it twists and bends. So He brought the higher closer to them by mentioning the lower that was known to them.

Take, for example, the date stone, which is of the least account, yet Allah honoured it when He mentioned from it three parts and made them illustrative examples. He mentioned the qitmir that we have in this verse, ﴿And those you invoke besides Him do not possess even a qitmir﴾ [Fatir: 13], which is the transparent membrane that surrounds the stone, and we find its like between the white of the egg and its shell.

And the mention of the naqir in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged even the amount of a naqir﴾ [al-Nisa': 124]. The naqir is a small hollow, or a dimple on the back of the stone.

And the mention of the fatil in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah; and you will not be wronged even the amount of a fatil﴾ [al-Nisa': 77].
