The fatil is a white thread that you find in the belly of the stone. These three: the qitmir, the naqir and the fatil, are struck as examples of a thing that is slight and extremely small.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿If you call them, they do not hear your call; and if they heard, they would not respond to you...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 14:

His words "If you call upon them" (in ﴿إِن تَدْعُوهُمْ﴾): here "du'a'" (supplication) means worship ('ibadah). Each of them would stand before his idol, calling upon it, seeking its intercession, and speaking to it, and so on. But far be it: this is a stone that does not hear, so calling upon it is foolishness, not to mention that it is disbelief. The meaning of ﴿لاَ يَسْمَعُواْ دُعَآءَكُمْ﴾ ("they would not hear your call") is: the deities, which do not understand and do not hear, such as trees, stones and other things.

But why did the disbelievers worship idols, for example, when they know that they are stones they carved with their own hands, and they see that a gust of wind knocks their deity over, throws it to the ground, and breaks its arm, so that it needs someone to repair it? It is a strange thing that idols are worshipped besides God. The reason, however, is the innate disposition of religiosity (fitrat al-tadayyun) in the human soul.

Every human being by nature loves religion. The affliction of religion is that it has requirements (matlubat). So what prevents a person from going to a form of religion that satisfies this innate disposition while having no requirements of him? From here idols were worshipped, and stars and trees were worshipped and made into gods.

The meaning of worship ('ibadah) is that the worshipper obeys the command of his worshipped object and refrains from its prohibition. So if there is no command and no prohibition, the worship is void and false, because you would be worshipping a god without a method (manhaj). Otherwise, what have these gods commanded them, and what have they forbidden them? What have they prepared for whoever worships them, and what have they prepared for whoever disbelieves in them?

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وَلَوْ سَمِعُواْ﴾ ("and if they heard"), meaning: on the supposition that they worshipped a human being who could hear them, ﴿مَا اسْتَجَابُواْ لَكُمْ﴾ ("they would not respond to you"), meaning: they would not agree to your worship of them, and they would reject being gods. An example of this: those who worshipped Jesus, peace be upon him, besides God...

The stone itself refuses to be worshipped besides God, and it knows in its reality the matter of tawhid, and it falls down prostrating to God, glorifying Him. So what about humans?

Therefore, on the Day of Resurrection we will see the wondrous disputes and arguments between worshipper and worshipped, and follower and followed. God, exalted is He, says:

﴿إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُواْ مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُواْ وَرَأَوُاْ الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الأَسْبَابُ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166] ("When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their means are cut off from them"). And He says, relating the words of those who went astray: ﴿رَبَّنَآ أَرِنَا الَّذَيْنِ أَضَلاَّنَا مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالإِنسِ نَجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِنَا لِيَكُونَا مِنَ الأَسْفَلِينَ﴾ [Fussilat: 29] ("Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and humankind, that we may place them beneath our feet so they will be among the lowest").

Here He, glorified is He, says: ﴿وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِـكُمْ﴾ [Fatir: 14] ("And on the Day of Resurrection they will disown your association"), meaning: those to whom you turned in worship and took as gods will disown you and your polytheism. ﴿وَلاَ يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ﴾ ("and none will inform you like one who is All-Aware"), meaning: one who knows the inner realities of matters. It is as if God, exalted is He, were saying to you: I inform you of what will be in the future, so take from My truthfulness regarding the past as evidence of My truthfulness regarding what is to come, and from My truthfulness regarding what you witness as evidence of My truthfulness regarding what is hidden from you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 35, verse 15:

The address "Yā ayyuhā al-nās" (O mankind) is a general address to all people, the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. ﴿You are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.﴾ This is a fact by which Allah humbles the pride of those who refuse to submit to belief in Allah and rebel against the methodology of Allah. It is as if Allah, exalted is He, is saying to them: Since you have become accustomed to rebellion, then rebel also against poverty if I make you poor, and against sickness if it befalls you, rebel against death if your term arrives. In short: you are subdued to the lordship of Allah, and you cannot be free of it.

﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.﴾ That is, absolute self-sufficiency (al-ghinā). The meaning of "al-Ḥamīd" is the one who is much praised. The self-sufficient is not praised unless he gives, and his giving is abundant; the self-sufficient who withholds is not praised but blamed.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 35, verses 16–17:

The address in ﴿O mankind﴾ [Fatir: 15] is a general address to all people, the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. ﴿You are the poor toward God, and God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15]. This is a truth by which God humbles the pride of those who refuse to believe in God and rebel against God's method. It is as if God, exalted is He, is saying to them: Since you have grown accustomed to rebellion, then rebel also against poverty if I impoverish you, and against sickness if it befalls you; rebel against death if your term comes. In sum, you are subdued to the lordship of God and cannot escape it.

﴿And God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15]. That is, absolute richness (al-ghina, self-sufficiency). The meaning of ﴿al-Hamid﴾ is "the one praised abundantly." Richness is not praised unless it gives, and its giving is abundant. The richness that withholds is not praised but blamed.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, reminds them of another truth that had been absent from them: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation﴾ [Fatir: 16]. As He said in another place: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. The meaning of "new creation": the new thing is one recently engaged in work, like a new garment, meaning one that has just been finished being sewn and has not yet been worn.

Restoring creation, or bringing a new creation, is an easy matter for God: ﴿And that is not difficult for God﴾ [Fatir: 17]. That is, it is not hard. However, the Truth, glorified is He, wants the creation to come to Him willingly, believing in Him, while they are able to disbelieve and have absolute choice. This choice is the locus of greatness in the religion of God.

We have previously illustrated this matter: if you had two slaves, and you held the first to you with a chain, and left the other free, and if you called out to either of them, the first would respond and answer. Which of them would be deemed more obedient to you? Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, wants us obedient by pleasure and by choice, not by compulsion and hatred. God, glorified is He, as we have said, does not want forms that submit; rather He wants hearts that humble themselves.

Bringing a new creation is an easy and simple matter for God, exalted is He, because God does not create by treatment; rather He creates by ﴿Be, and it is﴾. This, from God, requires no time.

If you wish to examine this meaning in His words: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82], you will find that the thing in reality already exists in fact, but in the world of the unseen and of command it has the capacity to appear to us in the world of actuality. Therefore, when one of the knowers was asked, he said: "Matters He manifests, and does not originate."

And you notice in His words ﴿And God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15] the mention of the separating pronoun (huwa). The Truth, glorified is He, did not say "and God the Self-Sufficient." This pronoun confirms the predicate and restricts richness to God, glorified and exalted is He. Therefore we have said that this pronoun comes only in places that may admit the suspicion of partnership, as in His words: ﴿He who created me, and He guides me. And He who feeds me and gives me drink. And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 78–80].

Here He used the third-person pronoun (huwa) because guidance, feeding, giving drink, and curing from illness are all matters in which one might suppose that someone among the creation shares with Him. As for speaking of death, He said: ﴿And He who causes me to die, then gives me life﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 81], and did not use the third-person pronoun here, because death and giving life belong to God alone; there is no suspicion in them, and no one has claimed them for himself.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative. You only warn...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 35, verses 16–17:

The address in ﴿O mankind﴾ [Fatir: 15] is a general address to all people, the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient. ﴿You are the poor toward God, and God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15]. This is a truth by which God humbles the pride of those who refuse to believe in God and rebel against God's method. It is as if God, exalted is He, is saying to them: Since you have grown accustomed to rebellion, then rebel also against poverty if I impoverish you, and against sickness if it befalls you; rebel against death if your term comes. In sum, you are subdued to the lordship of God and cannot escape it.

﴿And God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15]. That is, absolute richness (al-ghina, self-sufficiency). The meaning of ﴿al-Hamid﴾ is "the one praised abundantly." Richness is not praised unless it gives, and its giving is abundant. The richness that withholds is not praised but blamed.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, reminds them of another truth that had been absent from them: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation﴾ [Fatir: 16]. As He said in another place: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. The meaning of "new creation": the new thing is one recently engaged in work, like a new garment, meaning one that has just been finished being sewn and has not yet been worn.

Restoring creation, or bringing a new creation, is an easy matter for God: ﴿And that is not difficult for God﴾ [Fatir: 17]. That is, it is not hard. However, the Truth, glorified is He, wants the creation to come to Him willingly, believing in Him, while they are able to disbelieve and have absolute choice. This choice is the locus of greatness in the religion of God.

We have previously illustrated this matter: if you had two slaves, and you held the first to you with a chain, and left the other free, and if you called out to either of them, the first would respond and answer. Which of them would be deemed more obedient to you? Likewise, the Truth, glorified is He, wants us obedient by pleasure and by choice, not by compulsion and hatred. God, glorified is He, as we have said, does not want forms that submit; rather He wants hearts that humble themselves.

Bringing a new creation is an easy and simple matter for God, exalted is He, because God does not create by treatment; rather He creates by ﴿Be, and it is﴾. This, from God, requires no time.

If you wish to examine this meaning in His words: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82], you will find that the thing in reality already exists in fact, but in the world of the unseen and of command it has the capacity to appear to us in the world of actuality. Therefore, when one of the knowers was asked, he said: "Matters He manifests, and does not originate."

And you notice in His words ﴿And God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15] the mention of the separating pronoun (huwa). The Truth, glorified is He, did not say "and God the Self-Sufficient." This pronoun confirms the predicate and restricts richness to God, glorified and exalted is He. Therefore we have said that this pronoun comes only in places that may admit the suspicion of partnership, as in His words: ﴿He who created me, and He guides me. And He who feeds me and gives me drink. And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 78–80].

Here He used the third-person pronoun (huwa) because guidance, feeding, giving drink, and curing from illness are all matters in which one might suppose that someone among the creation shares with Him. As for speaking of death, He said: ﴿And He who causes me to die, then gives me life﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 81], and did not use the third-person pronoun here, because death and giving life belong to God alone; there is no suspicion in them, and no one has claimed them for himself.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative. You only warn...﴾

... Man in this world is bound either by kinship that carries rights over him, or by brothers and friends, or by a rescuer he seeks help from, even if he is neither a relative nor a friend. But on the Day of Resurrection all these bonds will be dissolved, because that standing does not admit of courtesies or sacrifices.

Therefore, when ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speaking to them about the Resurrection, and mentioning that the sun would draw near to the heads and that people would stand naked, she was dismayed and asked the Messenger of Allah: "How will people stand naked, with some looking at the private parts of others?" The Messenger of Allah answered her that every person would be preoccupied with himself, and that the matter is too great for anyone to look at another's nakedness in that situation.

Then He, glorified is He, says, addressing His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord in the unseen﴾. That is: your warning, O Muhammad, and your admonition benefit only those who fear their Lord in the unseen. As for the others, they have wronged themselves when they deprived themselves of the abundant good that Allah intended for them; they wronged themselves when the world deceived them with its perishing delights and distracted them from the enduring bliss of the Hereafter.

Warning (al-indhar, the act of alerting to evil before its time so that one may guard against it) is making one fear an evil before its arrival, so that one may avoid it while the opportunity is still at hand. For example, when you want to urge your son to study and warn him against the negligence that leads to failure, you do not tell him this on the night of the examination; rather you tell him well in advance, so that he has enough time to rectify his situation and correct whatever shortcoming or negligence he has.

Warning and admonition are of no use except to one who believes in what you warn him of. So when the Messenger of Allah warns of the punishment of the Hereafter, only those who believe in Allah and believe in the Resurrection benefit from that warning.

As for the meaning of ﴿those who fear their Lord﴾: khashya (fear accompanied by reverence) is fear, but with love and veneration, not fear born of hatred. For example, you may fear a cruel tyrant, but you fear him while hating him. Your fear of Allah, however, is a fear that results from love and veneration. Therefore this fear is accompanied by hope and longing for His mercy, may He be exalted. You travel the journey of your life with two wings: fear of punishment and hope in mercy.

A person should not look at an act in itself alone, but should look at the act and at the one who receives it. The same act may have different outcomes... Likewise, His warning, may He bless him and grant him peace, is one warning, yet a people received it with submission and desire for guidance, so they believed; and another people received it with obstinacy and insistence, so they did not benefit from it and did not gain its fruit.

His saying ﴿those who fear their Lord in the unseen﴾ indicates that faith was complete in the hearts of these people, to a degree in which the unseen and the seen are equal. Among such statements is the saying of the Imam ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him): "Were the veil removed from me, I would not increase in certainty..."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, mentions another attribute of those who responded to the warning of the Messenger of Allah and benefited from it: ﴿and they establish the prayer﴾. So, along with their fear of Allah, which brought them to a faith in which the unseen is equal to the witnessed, they also establish the prayer, that is, they perform it in the most complete manner. As we have mentioned, prayer is the only act of worship that never falls from the responsible person under any circumstance. Zakat may fall away from you, or fasting, or Hajj, and nothing remains except the testimony that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. This is enough: you need only say it once.

As for prayer, it is the act of worship that constantly accompanies the Muslim, because prayer in its reality is the continuous renewal of allegiance to Allah, may He be exalted. Your Lord invites you to meet Him five times a day and night; He calls you to present the creation to its Creator. So what of a creation that is presented to its Creator five times a day and night? Could there be any defect in it after that?

If you wish to meet a great one of this world, there are gates, guards, appointments and strict procedures before him, and you own none of the elements of that meeting; rather, the time, the subject, and even what you say are determined for you. You ask permission at the beginning and you cannot leave at the end whenever you wish.

But your meeting with your Lord is different: in your hand are all the elements of the meeting. You begin it whenever you like, end it as you like, and converse with your Lord in it about whatever you want. You pour out your complaint to Him and present your need, and He hears and responds.

After the Truth, glorified is He, has mentioned this constant act, He establishes this reality: ﴿And whoever purifies himself, purifies himself only for his own sake﴾. That is: your worship returns to you; Allah, may He be exalted, gains nothing from it. He is not benefited by the obedience of the obedient, nor harmed by the disobedience of the disobedient.

He, glorified is He, is independent of us. By our worship of Allah we have added to Him no attribute of perfection that He did not already have, because it is by His attribute of perfection that He brought us into existence and by His attribute of perfection that He imposed obligations upon us. Therefore a sacred hadith states: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, your present and your absent, were all upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in anything. And if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, your present and your absent, were all upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in anything. For I am Generous, Glorious, Finder; My giving is a word, and My punishment is a word. My command, when I intend a thing, is only that I say to it 'Be,' and it is."

So: we are the creation of Allah. We have never seen a maker who sets about his creation to destroy or spoil it; rather he repairs it, refines it, and takes care of it. Even if harm or pain befalls you, know that in the end it is for your benefit.

﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾. That is: the place of return and the final destination on the Day of Resurrection, where He will judge between the adversaries and every soul will receive what it deserves. Whoever escapes punishment in this world, there is a return to which he will come back.

This is a set of truths established by the Truthful Lord (al-Haqq, subhanahu). Opposites are not equal: the blind man does not know the positions of things as he moves, whereas the seeing man knows the positions of things as he moves. The seeing man sees the positions of things and avoids dangers. As for the blind man, he must have a companion who volunteers to lend his sound eye to the absent eye. Therefore we say: if the blind man gives blindness its due, he becomes one who sees. How? Because he does not feel too proud to seek the help of the one who sees. So when he calls out to whoever will take his hand, all the eyes around him rush to help him; but if he becomes arrogant, he quickly stumbles on his face.

Blindness and sight are sensory matters that clarify the non-sensory. The meaning is that the ignorant and the knowing are not equal, because the movement of life is divided into material movement, which comes and goes, sows and uproots, etc., and value-based, non-material movement, which is spiritual and lofty moral matters, such as the meanings of faith, truthfulness, loyalty, justice, mercy, etc.

If sensory material movement needs sensory light that guides you so that you do not collide with what is stronger than you and so it crushes you, or with what is weaker than you and so you crush it, then likewise spiritual, non-material value-based movement needs non-material light that guides your steps so that you do not go astray. This non-material light is the methodology (al-manhaj) about which Allah said:

﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book. Allah guides by it whoever pursues His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out of darknesses into the light by His permission and guides them to a straight path.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 15-16].

So the sun is the sensory light, and the Qur'an is the non-material light. Therefore we said, regarding the Most High's saying: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Nur: 35], that is: the One who illuminates them with the two lights.

The Truthful Lord had earlier mentioned the contrast between the two waters, the sweet and the salty, saying: ﴿And not equal are the two seas - this one sweet, fresh, pleasant for drinking, and this one salty and bitter﴾. Yes, they are not equal, but the relationship between them is one of complementarity (taqabul), like the night and the day, not one of contradiction (tadadd), like the blind and the seeing, as evidenced by the fact that Allah joined them together, saying: ﴿And from each you eat tender meat and extract ornaments which you wear﴾ [Fatir: 12]. So if the two complementary things differ, each of them has a task it performs; they are mutually supportive, not mutually opposing.

After the Truthful Lord mentioned that the blind and the seeing are not equal, He says: ﴿Nor are darknesses and light﴾ [Fatir: 20], because light is the source of sight, so the one who sees sees nothing in darkness.

This is in the case of sensory blindness and sight; as for values and non-material matters, they have another measure. Therefore the Most High says: ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [al-Hajj: 46]. A man may be sighted and yet be blind in insight (a'ma basirah). The one who is blind in non-material matters is the one who is ignorant of the ruling that guides him to the region of truth in all values, and the one who sees is the one who knows these rulings.

When you reflect on the style of these two verses, you find in them a feature of the inimitability (i'jaz) of Allah's speech. The first, ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing﴾ [Fatir: 19], joins the two with the conjunctive waw; while the other, ﴿Nor are darknesses and light﴾ [Fatir: 20], mentions the negating (la) which indicates emphasis on non-equality. The Truthful Lord did not say, as in the first, "nor the darknesses and the light." Why?

They said: because blindness and sight are two attributes that may be combined in one person; he may be blind today and see tomorrow, ignorant and then learning, or disbelieving and then believing, so both attributes may apply to him. Therefore non-equality was not emphasized. As for darknesses and light, they are complementary and cannot be combined.

You also notice the precision of the Qur'anic expression: because the Truthful Lord is the Speaker, He said: ﴿Nor are darknesses and light﴾ [Fatir: 20]. "Darknesses" is plural and "light" is singular, because the paths of misguidance are many: this one worships the stars, that one worships idols, another worships the angels, etc. As for light, it is one: it is the methodology of God revealed in His Book.

Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to teach his companions this lesson, he drew for them a straight line, with crooked lines around it, then recited: ﴿And that this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] paths, lest they separate you from His way﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

Then He says: ﴿Nor is shade and heat﴾ [Fatir: 21], and these too are complementary and cannot be combined. Likewise: ﴿And not equal are the living and the dead﴾ [Fatir: 22]. You notice here that the Truthful Lord repeated the negated verb "and not equal" (wa ma yastawi) [Fatir: 22] to emphasize the non-equality between the living and the dead.

Similarly, He mentioned the negating "la" which indicates emphasis, because the word "the living" means the believers with true faith, who deserve an everlasting life connected to their transient worldly life; while "the dead" are the disbelievers who refused the methodology of God. Or: the living are those who know that true life is living by the methodology of their Lord, which leads them to the real, enduring life about which Allah said:

﴿And indeed, the Hereafter - that is the real life, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64].

This is the life intended in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when He calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. How [can it be meant as life in the ordinary sense], when He is addressing them while they are already living? Therefore the meaning is: that which gives you the real life that does not end in death, and from which no blessing is removed.

Also among this is His saying: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darknesses, never to emerge from them?﴾ [al-An'am: 122].

Among the meanings we understand from the non-equality of the living and the dead is that the living was created by God and equipped with psychological faculties: intellect, nerves, muscles, hearing and sight, etc. These organs have value and purpose, and he must use these blessings in a way that makes them means to other blessings. Then let him know that in the journey of his life he will certainly die, but his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, concealed his term from him so that this would be a clear sign, and so that he would remain mindful of it at all times and await it in every moment. Your lifespan is counted by a countdown, and the arrow of death has already been shot in your direction; your life is measured by the time of its arrival to you.

"The shade" is a metaphor for the bliss of Paradise, and in another place He said: ﴿Shade extended﴾ [al-Nisa: 57]; and "al-harur" is a metaphor for punishment and its intense heat.

Among the meanings we understand from the non-equality of the living and the dead is that the living one, whom Allah created and equipped with psychological faculties—intellect, nerves, muscles, hearing and sight, etc.—these organs have value and a purpose, and he must use these blessings in a way that makes them means to other blessings. Then let him know that in the journey of his life he will certainly die, but his Lord, mighty and majestic, kept his term hidden from him so that this would be a clear sign, and so that he remains mindful of it at all times, awaiting it at every moment. Your life is counted down like a countdown, and the arrow of death has already been shot in your direction, and your life is by the measure of its reaching you.

After the Real, glory be to Him, spoke about the state in terms of obligations, saying: the blind man ignorant of the foundations of his religion and the seeing man who knows them are not equal, nor is the light of faith and guidance equal to the darknesses of misguidance, He, glory be to Him, now speaks about the outcome, saying: ﴿Nor is the shade and the heat﴾ [Fatir: 21]. "The shade" is a metaphor for the bliss of Paradise, and in another place He said:

﴿Permanent shade﴾ [al-Nisa': 57], and "the heat" is a metaphor for punishment and its intense heat.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says, addressing His Prophet ﷺ and consoling him: ﴿Indeed, Allah makes hear whom He wills, and you cannot make hear those who are in the graves.﴾ The Prophet ﷺ came to a people in disbelief and ignorance, so his call was to bring them out of blindness and ignorance to that which illuminates their insight, and to bring them out of the darkness of misguidance to the light of faith.

The Prophet ﷺ was exceedingly eager for the guidance of his people, nearly destroying himself in the cause of his call. Therefore his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps, if they do not believe in this message, in sorrow.﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]

Likewise here He addresses him saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah makes hear whom He wills﴾, meaning the hearing of guidance and acceptance. Otherwise, they all hear, but there is the hearing of aversion and the hearing of acceptance. Among them are those who accept, believe, and are moved by the speech of Allah, and among them are those who hear and then turn away and depart from what they heard. Therefore Allah said concerning them: ﴿And had Allah known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse.﴾ [al-Anfal: 23]

So the meaning is: O Muhammad, you have discharged your duty towards them. You addressed them with the address of guidance and the address of warning and threat, but they did not hear. ﴿And you cannot make hear those who are in the graves﴾; so Allah, because of their not hearing, made them like the dead. Otherwise, "the Messenger of Allah addressed the people of the well of Badr from among the disbelievers when he stood over them and called them by their names: 'O Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, O Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, O Abu Jahl, did you not find what your Lord promised you to be true? Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true.'"

Umar said: "Do you speak to them when they have decayed?" He ﷺ said: "By Allah, you are not more hearing than them, but they cannot respond."

So the meaning is: you cannot make hear the hearing that leads to guidance, just as you cannot make hear those in the graves, because the time for hearing and accepting guidance has ended with death.

But if the Messenger of Allah cannot make hear those in the graves, what then is his mission? Allah, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿You are only a warner.﴾

In this verse, *in* (إنْ) is used in the sense of the negative *ma* (ما): "You are only a warner" (ما أنت إلا نذير), meaning: one who warns against disobedience and against punishment. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, wishes to lighten the burden on His Messenger by defining his task as this alone. He is not to add to it what burdens him so much that he almost destroys himself. So He tells him: your task is only warning, while guidance is from God, so ease your soul. Had God willed to make them all believers, they would have come obediently and subjugated, like the other creatures. ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief that they do not become believers.﴾ ﴿If We willed, We would send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks would remain humbly bowed before it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 3-4].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth, as a bringer of good news and a warner...﴾.

Al-Haqq (the truth): it is that which is firm and does not change. Allah, exalted is He, sets forth for us a sensory example to clarify truth and falsehood, so He says:

﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from that which they heat in the fire, seeking an ornament or goods, there is a foam like it. Thus Allah sets forth truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but as for that which benefits people, it remains on the earth. Thus Allah sets forth the parables﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17].

We have rendered this relationship between truth and falsehood into a contemporary expression, saying: "Only the genuine survives," yes, because falsehood, even if it takes the form of truth for a time, is like the foam which the winds soon sweep away, to reveal the bright face of reality and the clear truth.

As for His saying to His Prophet: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾ it indicates that he is the final Messenger, after whom there is no messenger or prophet, who changes nothing of what he brought. The Prophet brought the firm truth that never changes, and no one after him may amend it. Therefore, the plague of humanity now is that it judges the age and adapts circumstances in ruling on violations of the Shari'ah. When we confront a violation, we hear someone say that it is the inevitable development, and these are the advocates of "modernizing" (ʿaṣrana) religion, meaning bending religion to suit the age.

This means that the development of the age becomes the legislator, whereas it should be that the age receives the legislation of heaven and builds its life movement upon its guidance and light; for the movement built upon the guidance of heaven is the supreme movement from the Lord Most High, who knows the reality of good for you and is not corrected by anyone. But if a human like you legislates for you, even if he points you to good, it is good from his own viewpoint and according to the measure of his knowledge; there must be in it deficiency and shortcoming, and there must come after him someone who overturns it and amends it.

Therefore we have seen that even non-Muslims, whom the exigencies of life compel, take up the solutions of Islam to overcome their problems, and they of course do not take the rulings of Islam out of love for it, but only because they have found no solution outside it. Among these issues is the matter of divorce, about which they often raised doubts and considered it a criticism of Islam; and now in Italy they legislate divorce, not because Islam prescribed it, but because their problems cannot be solved except by it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 25:

Meaning: O Muhammad, take for yourself an example from your brother messengers before you, for they were all denied. This is a established practice (sunnah muttaba'ah), and you, O Muhammad, are no novelty among the messengers. We have said that Allah the Exalted does not send a messenger except when corruption has spread widely and the remedy has become scarce. There is no longer any self that blames (al-nafs al-lawwamah) that restrains its owner from sin, nor any society that enjoins good and forbids evil (al-amr bi'l-ma'ruf wa'l-nahy 'an al-munkar). That is to say: there is no immunity within the self and no immunity within society, for society too has become corrupt, and its people have united in error. At that point, heaven must intervene with a new messenger who brings a miracle suited to the age in which he comes.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if they deny you, then those before them had denied [their messengers] too﴾ [Fatir: 25], this is because the messenger comes only to confront corruption in society. It is natural that the misguided, the wrongdoers, the tyrants, and those who profit from this corruption confront him and deny him. For this reason, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus We have placed in every town its greatest criminals to plot therein﴾ [al-An'am: 123].

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Their messengers came to them with the clear proofs﴾ [Fatir: 25]. "Clear proofs" means: the evident thing that makes clear that the speaker is truthful in conveying and delivering the message of his Lord. This is the miracle. Thus, the messenger came with a miracle to be a proof of his truthfulness in delivering the message of his Lord. The miracle is not the goal of the message; rather, the goal of the message is to convey the rulings and the method.

And His saying ﴿and the scriptures﴾ [Fatir: 25] means: the heavenly books that were sent down, such as the scrolls of Ibrahim (suhuf Ibrahim), the Torah of Musa, and the Gospel of 'Isa. However, here He singled out the Zabur and the Qur'an, (the zubur and the illuminating Book), because the Zabur that was sent down to our master Dawud was distinguished by being written, written with letters engraved in relief, and therefore it was fixed and not with ink that can be erased, for example. It is closer to stone inscriptions, and they call it (al-Uwaymah).

And the illuminating Book is the noble Qur'an, because it is the spiritual light that illuminates for people the path of life and guides their movement. If the sun is the sensory light that guides your movement among sensible things, then the Qur'an is the spiritual light that guides whoever believes in it.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved...﴾.

This is the Sunnah of Allah concerning the messengers: that He seizes those among the disbelievers who oppose them and rebel against them. Have you seen a prophet whom Allah abandoned, or who was defeated before his obstinate people? Allah promised His Messenger victory and support, and He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾ [Ghafir: 51].

And He said: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will be the victorious﴾ [As-Saffat: 173]. Therefore, if you see a soldier of Allah defeated in something and not victorious, know that one of the conditions of soldiership was not fulfilled, and the first condition of soldiership to Allah is obedience. If the soldier disobeys the commands of Allah, he will inevitably be defeated. For this reason we said: the Muslims were victorious at Badr while they were a small group,

﴿How many a small group has overcome a large group by the permission of Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 249].

Not a single year had passed since Badr when Uhud occurred. It is true that the Muslims were not defeated, but neither were they victorious, because the battle was "confused" (ma'at, i.e., it turned into disorder). This was because the archers disobeyed the order of the Messenger of Allah, abandoned their positions, and descended to collect the spoils. Allah, exalted is He, wished to discipline His sincere servants, so He had to shake them with this violent jolt and let them see this outcome, because they had disobeyed.

For this reason we said: Islam was victorious at Uhud, even though the Muslims did not win. Had they won while disobeying the Messenger's command, the commands of the Messenger would have become insignificant to the Muslims afterwards, and they would have said: "We disobeyed his orders and still won at Uhud." Thus, this confused outcome was necessary, so that the Muslims would know the importance of obedience and of following the example of the Messenger...

When we reflect on the meaning of ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved﴾, we find that al-akhdh (seizing) indicates the strength of the seizer and a pull that encompasses every part of the one seized. On the human level, we say: "Akhadha fulan" means he seized him by his collar or pulled him by the fold of his garment and held him with a grip of his hand. But if you say "Allah seized him," then Allah's seizing is severe: a seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

Therefore He says after it: ﴿So how was My rejection?﴾ i.e., My rejection and My objection to what they did. Al-nakir (rejection) is the thing you disapprove of and become angry about. What then of a people whose conduct Allah has rejected and against whom He is angry? He must seize them with a seizing that pleases His allies and pleases the believers in Him.

So His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿So how was My rejection?﴾ means: Tell me, O Muhammad, were you able to requite them with what they deserve? This meaning is also clear in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their families, they would return jesting. And when they saw them, they would say, "Indeed, these are the astray." But they had not been sent as overseers over them. So today, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers not been repaid for what they used to do?﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin: 29–36].

You notice that the Exalted Lord reminds us of some of His favours upon us, then follows that with some of the things He requires of us, and so on, in order to comfort your heart with His kindness toward you, so that you respond to what He requires. When the Exalted Lord reminds His servants of this cosmic sign, the sign of the sending down of water from the sky, after having shown His Prophet His severe seizing of the disbelievers, it is as though He, glorified is He, says to His Messenger: Leave aside the matter of these disbelievers, for I am able to punish them. And reflect on this cosmic sign: ﴿Do you not see that God sends down water from the sky, and with it We bring forth fruits of varying colours?﴾

His saying ﴿Do you not see﴾ means: do you not witness? For everyone sees water descending from the high place. The sky (samaʾ) is everything that is above you and shades you. The phrase ﴿Do you not see﴾ may also come in the sense of "Do you not know," as in ﴿Do you not see how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?﴾ (105:1). It is well known that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not witness the incident of the Elephant, yet his Lord addressed him with ﴿Do you not see﴾ to show that God's report to him is more certain and more truthful than seeing with the eye.

As for the matter of the sending down of water from the sky, that is, from its direction, since the sky is something else; rain only descends from the clouds that are near the earth. We say: the matter of water descending from the direction of the sky appears to be a natural matter. Water vapour condenses in the sky in the form of clouds full of water, and water has weight that makes it descend downward by the pull of the earth's gravity. Therefore God makes the sending down of rain lead to the bringing forth of vegetation: ﴿So We bring forth with it fruits of varying colours﴾ (35:27). If you say: the descent of water from the sky is a natural matter that may be doubted as being the work of nature, then is the revival of the earth and the growth of plants of varying fruits and colours also the work of nature?

The word anzala (He sent down) indicates height on the part of the one who sends down and nearness to the one to whom it is sent down, even if this matter is reversed and the sending down comes from below to above, as in His saying: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for mankind﴾ (57:25). In reality iron is extracted from within the earth, yet God called it a sending down, because what is meant by it is coming from a higher place to a lower one, regardless of whether its direction is up or down.

We witness the process of water descending from the sky, but we have not witnessed the process of evaporation that takes place on the surface of the water on the earth, then its rising to the upper layers of the atmosphere where clouds form through condensation. Man knew nothing of these processes until sciences advanced and we came to know the process of distilling water.

As for the process of bringing forth vegetation and fruits of varying colours, it is clearly witnessed in orchards and fields. Everyone sees the marvellous colours and the variety of shapes, to such an extent that they cannot be counted; for if the colours of the spectrum are the primary colours, then from them can be produced what is beyond counting. The colour black, for example, if you add one drop of brown to it, gives you another colour; if you add two drops, it gives you a third colour, and so on, and the colours become endless. We see this matter now in the manufacture of fabrics, whose colours have multiplied in different shades and embroideries that cannot be counted.

So we say: colours are a thing that cannot be exhausted.

You may reflect on the blending and harmony of colours in a flower or a rose in the garden, and you will see in its colours a dazzling inimitability (iʿjaz, the quality of being beyond human ability to match). The seed is one, the earth is one, and the water is one, yet from all of this there emerges this wonderful shape and these blended, harmonious colours. This is because the event bears the traces of its originator. If the originator is limited in power, its traces appear limited in power too; if the originator is supremely powerful, its traces come supremely powerful. As for the Exalted Lord, He has absolute power, so His traces are likewise.

You notice in the context of the verse that the Exalted Lord did not speak of the sending down of rain by saying "He sent down" (anzala) in the third-person singular form. But when He spoke of bringing forth the fruits He said ﴿We bring forth﴾ (fa-akhrajna), shifting to the first-person plural which indicates glorification. Why? Because the sending down of water from the sky is not an aim in itself; it is not the important thing. This is evident from the fact that water may fall on saline land, and then it benefits nothing. But the process of bringing forth fruits is the important process for which God sent down the water. Therefore He mentioned it with the plural pronoun that indicates glorification. The Exalted Lord glorifies Himself in the act, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardian﴾ (15:9).

Thus we find that when the Exalted Lord speaks to us of one of His acts, He speaks to us with the plural pronoun; but if He speaks of His own Self, glorified is He, He speaks with the singular pronoun, as in:

﴿Indeed, I am God; there is no god but I, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ (20:14).

The sending down of water, in its form, is one matter; but the bringing forth involves variation in what is brought forth. The water sent down from the sky is one, but the effects of the water are many: this is yellow, this is white, this is red, and so on. This process therefore requires glorification that suits it.

But is the bringing forth of fruits directly like this? Or is it the bringing forth of the plant that gives the fruits? It is the bringing forth of the plant that gives fruit. The Exalted Lord mentions the thing by its final purpose, which is the fruit, and this fruit comes differing in its colours, although the environment is one and it is watered with one water. And when you reflect on the colours of fruits, you find in them the absolute power of God, the Exalted. These colours were not made this way merely for shape and adornment; rather they were made this way for a wisdom that the Creator, glorified is He, intended, among which is that these colours attract the pollinating insects.

If you reflect on these colours, you will find them multiple even within a single colour. Do you not see that the whiteness of snow, for example, differs from the whiteness of a garment, and from the whiteness of lime? For this reason they describe colours saying: "bright white (abyad yaqiq), intense yellow (asfar faqiʿ), deep red (ahmar qani), and dark green (akhdar mudhamm)."

After the Exalted Lord has told us of one of His signs in plants, He tells us of inanimate things: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying hues, and jet-black﴾ (35:27). In inanimate things too there are colours that we witness, for example when we split rock to extract what is within the earth's depths: you see, for instance, granite, marble, and agate in various colours likewise.

The word judad (streaks) in the verse is the plural of judda, which is the dividing line between two things. You have surely seen the striped wild donkey and the extent of the harmony of its stripes. You see the like of this in the layers of mountains, which differ in whiteness and differ in redness.

As for the meaning of ﴿jet-black﴾ (ghirabib sud): you say "aswad ghirbib," meaning: intensely black. Ghirbib is the most intense degree of blackness, relative to the crow (ghurab), because of its intense blackness.

Therefore, difference exists in all kinds of created things, because creation rests upon the absoluteness of power (ṭalāqat al-qudra). People, despite their great number, are different from one another, and this is a miracle that points to the absoluteness of power. Creation is not cast in a single mould that produces identical copies. You look at a man and say he resembles so-and-so, but if you examine closely you will surely see a difference. Therefore, the absoluteness of power requires that all kinds of existence differ: the inanimate, the plants, the animals, and humankind.

The meaning of al-dawābb (the creatures that crawl): every creature that crawls upon the earth, except humankind and the cattle (al-an'ām), which are the cows, the sheep, the camels, and the goats.

As for His, glorified be He, saying: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾...

Khashya (fear) is fear mingled with hope. Among the scholars, this is one of the deeds of the hearts. You may fear your enemy, for example, but you have no hope in him. Whereas when you fear Allah, you fear Him, glorified be He, while you hope in Him and love Him. Therefore they said: there is no refuge from Allah except unto Him.

Knowledge is of two kinds: sharʿī knowledge (ʿilm sharʿī), which is the knowledge of the rulings: the lawful, the unlawful, the obligatory, the recommended, and so on; or knowledge of the cosmos (al-kawniyyāt). This verse came in the context of speaking about cosmic signs, and nothing before it mentioned any of the rulings of the Sharia. Therefore we say that what is meant by "the scholars" here is the scholars of the cosmos and natural phenomena. It is fitting that these be the people most fearful of Allah, Exalted is He, because they know best the cosmic signs in the inanimate things, in plants, in animals, and in humankind, and they are the most capable of deriving from these signs the secrets of Allah, Exalted is He.

The cosmos is the proof of the Necessary Existent (wājib al-wujūd), and it is the gateway to reaching the Creator, glorified be He, and to belief in Him. Therefore we often find in the Qur'an:

﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen﴾ [al-Rūm: 23].

When knowledge is a certain matter, affirmed and supported by evidence, the Truthful, glorified and exalted be He, has sent down to us the knowledge of the Sharia and has set its limits for us, so we have no say in it. Therefore Allah has protected it and made it firm, because desires differ regarding it. The Truthful, glorified be He, says:

﴿Had the truth followed their desires, the heavens and the earth would have been corrupted﴾ [al-Mu'minūn: 71]. As for the knowledge of the cosmos, the Creator, glorified be He, has left it to minds to investigate, to derive from, and to compete in; indeed, some states even steal it from others...

As for His, exalted be He, saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is Mighty, Forgiving﴾: Mighty, not overcome; and Forgiving to you if there occurs from you forgetfulness or shortcoming in deriving the secrets of Allah in His creation. He forgives them if they err in one of their experiments, for those who come after them will come and correct it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 29:

After Allah, glorified is He, mentioned cosmic knowledge, and that it is a means to fear Allah and to know His secrets in His creation, He, glorified is He, wanted to draw our attention and to warn us: beware lest you be tempted by cosmic knowledge so that it makes you forget your mission of receiving from Allah what makes you happy. So He, glorified is He, spoke of the method: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah﴾, and this is the sacred knowledge and the remembrance that protects people from the discord of desires.

The meaning of ﴿recite the Book of Allah﴾ is: their tongues are constantly engaged with it, and their hearts comprehend it. ﴿And establish prayer﴾, and this is an act of worship in which all the limbs participate. ﴿And spend out of what We have provided for them, secretly and openly﴾. Spending (infaq) pertains to the financial aspect; it is evidence of the generosity of the soul with what it spends, and its love for giving and bestowing, in secret and in public. Through spending, these good qualities are completed for this soul, and the work of the heart and the work of the limbs gather for it in obedience to Allah.

His saying ﴿out of what We have provided for them﴾ means: spending is not from your own property, but from the property of Allah, who provided it for you and made you a steward over it. Your spending is only a means, and means in the universe are a veil over the hand of Allah in giving.

And those who spend out of what Allah has provided them, secretly and openly, ﴿hope for a commerce that will never perish﴾.

So spending in the way of Allah is a commerce with Allah ﴿that will never perish﴾, that is, will never go slack. When you spend on the needy, and when you feed the hungry, you are in fact making Allah beloved to His creation. Consider: if a king of the kings of the world has servants, is he not responsible for feeding them and meeting their needs? This is one of the marks of his greatness. Likewise, Allah, glorified is He, is the Creator of these poor people; He is the One who summoned them into existence, and He, glorified is He, is the One responsible for providing their sustenance.

Therefore: when you feed them, it is as if you are performing the task of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, and making the creatures of Allah beloved to Allah. When Allah, glorified is He, shows compassion to one creature toward another, He says: "It is as if My servant is helping Me with My creation," because Allah, exalted is He, summoned creation into existence and undertook to enrich them. So when His wealthy servant comes and aids the poor, He, glorified is He, says: "My servant was helping his brother by My power, so I must necessarily be helping him by My power." The servant is never more noble than his Creator. How could a servant show compassion when he has created nothing and summoned no one into existence, while the Creator, glorified is He, does not show compassion?

If you say: since Allah, glorified is He, has summoned creation into existence, why did He not guarantee for them a noble life in which they would not need anyone's compassion other than His?

We say: Allah, glorified is He, wanted to sow the seeds of love and mutual compassion among His creatures. He wanted a Muslim society founded on love, on cooperation, and on mutual social solidarity. Then He, glorified is He, promised the generous, bountiful giver that He would deal with him according to the measure of his generosity and giving, which is His own.

This is the commerce with Allah that never perishes. "Perishing" (al-baur) and "al-bawar" mean corruption, and it afflicts commerce from two directions: either corruption in the profit, such that the trade wearies you and yields no gain, or corruption in both profit and capital, meaning you lose the principal of the trade. It is well known that a person does not trade except with the intention of profit. Therefore the people of knowledge and the people of commerce with Allah have said: If you want certain profit, then trade with a Generous One who grants you what you give and then rewards you for it.

Thus one of the righteous would welcome the beggar with a smile and a cheerful face, saying to him: "Welcome to one who has come to carry my provision to the Hereafter without a fee."

And Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked: "O Abu al-Hasan, I wish to know myself: am I of the people of this world or of the people of the Hereafter?" He said: "If you are pleased with the one who gives you more than the one who takes from you, then you are of the people of this world, because a person loves whoever develops what he loves..."

The use of the negative particle (lan) here has a nuance: ﴿lan﴾ negates both the present and the future, because a person may die before he attains the fruit of good in this giving, and before he sees the result of his sincerity. Therefore his Lord reassures him that this is a commerce with Allah that will never perish, and its reward awaits him in the Hereafter. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿secretly and openly﴾ [Fatir: 29] means: in any state. As for secret spending, its wisdom is that it keeps its giver away from showing off or seeking to be seen, and it is also a veil over the modesty of the recipient. Therefore some of the knowers, when they wished to show compassion to a poor or needy person, would employ a stratagem that preserves the needy person's dignity: for example, they would assign him a simple task and then give him money as his wage for the work, not as charity.

Some act with courtesy in this matter, giving the needy person the money as a loan while intending it as charity...

And some give charity as a trust, but tell the recipient: "If this amount becomes available to you and exceeds your need, give it to someone in need of it, and tell him to give it in turn to whoever needs it after him," and thus charity multiplies and circulates among the needy for as long as Allah wills.

This concerns secret charity. As for open charity, its wisdom is that it serves as a deterrent to the wealthy so that he does not withhold or grudge what he has. It also protects its giver from people's tongues, and protects his honor from people discussing his conduct, saying: "He is stingy despite his wealth." Moreover, open spending serves as a model and exemplar for others in giving.

The scholars said: "secret" refers to voluntary charity beyond the obligatory, which should be concealed, and "open" refers to the obligatory zakat, because openness is desirable in worship, as is the case with prayer for instance. A reflective person will find that zakat is more fitting for openness than prayer, for it is easy to establish prayer at its times, whereas with zakat you may be wealthy yet your soul is miserly and withholds the giving.

And when you spend, whom do you spend on? On a needy person who is unable or deprived of ability. And who deprived him of ability? Allah. Therefore Allah has obligated you to spend on the one whom He deprived of ability, and to help him: first, so that he does not harbor resentment against you, and so that he wishes you more good, since your good will return to him. This is why we used to see people of the countryside, for example, grieve and weep if the cow of so-and-so or the buffalo of so-and-so died, why? Because it used to give the poor drink from its milk and plough the land of the needy.

Second: this is a wisdom more sublime than the first, namely that spending on one who is unable keeps him from altering his thoughts about his Lord and Creator, and protects him from objecting to the decree of Allah, who withheld from him and gave to others, and restricted him while expanding for others.

Spending on one who is unable makes him feel that he is in a better state than the wealthy, and why not, when his provision is brought to him without effort or toil on his part, and wealth comes to his door to give him his right in the property of Allah. Therefore the scholars said: "The poor person is a condition of the faith of the rich, and the rich is not a condition of the faith of the poor."

Thus our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), taught us, saying: "...and a man who gave charity and concealed it, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives."

When Allah, the Exalted, spoke of those who do good and burden themselves beyond what Allah has obligated them with, and of the same kind as what He obligated them with, He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good. They used to sleep but little at night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness, and in their wealth was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 15-19].

So the known right is the charity, whereas the obligatory zakat, which is the right of the poor in the wealth of the rich, is mentioned among the attributes of the believers in the surah of the Ma'arij, where He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And those in whose wealth is a known right, for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 25].

Therefore zakat is not hidden; rather it is paid openly, because you are paying a right you owe to the poor. Indeed, one of the jurists of al-Andalus, may Allah be pleased with them, said: "If I were entrusted with authority over the believers, and I saw someone withholding from the poor his right in the amount of a nisab, I would come to him to cut off his hand." Reflect on this ijtihad of the scholars, and how they equated withholding the poor man's right with theft.

Whether spending is secret or open and public, sincere intention must necessarily be present...

And in your giving you deal with Allah, and Allah is All-Finding, All-Glorious, Generous, who does not diminish your right, and your commerce with Him, glorified is He, must necessarily be profitable. Therefore He said after it: ﴿They hope for a commerce that will never perish﴾ [Fatir: 29].

Then He, glorified is He, says: "That He may pay them their rewards in full and increase them of His bounty." That is: they will receive the recompense of their deeds and their gifts in full from God, and then He will increase them beyond that out of His bounty, through generosity. They said this increase is that their intercession is accepted for those they love: if they intercede for one of their beloved ones, God accepts their intercession. Why? Because they have previous favours (ayadin sabiqah) upon the poor and needy among God's servants, for which God honours them, and He grants them His favour just as they showed favour to His servants.

"Indeed, He is Forgiving, Grateful." ﴿Indeed, He is Forgiving, Grateful.﴾

You may ask: why was the verse concluded with the Name "the Forgiving" (al-Ghafur), even though it speaks of acts of goodness: reciting the Book of God, establishing prayer, and spending in the way of God? Which of these needs forgiveness?

They said: forgiveness is mentioned here because when the servant performs some of this good, there may enter into it some vanity, self-admiration, or other things that taint righteous deeds, so God forgives it for him, so that he receives his reward purely...

As for His saying "Grateful" (Shakur), it is an intensive form (sigha mubalaghah) of "grateful" (shakir). It is as if God, in His majesty, thanks His servant, and even exaggerates in thanking him; because the servant, on the surface of the matter, has assisted his Lord in providing for the one whom God was asked to provide for; therefore God thanks him and does not diminish his due, although in reality he is merely a conduit (munawil) from God.

And when you recite it, "Indeed, He is Forgiving, Grateful," and you know that He, exalted is He, thanks you, you cannot but thank Him, glorified is He, and then He increases you in blessing. Thus we are before a constant gratitude that never ends, and a giving that never runs out.

Revelation, in its general sense, as we have said, is notification in concealment. If it were open and public, it would not be called revelation. For example, a group of guests enters upon you and you glance merely once at your servant, and he understands from it what you want without anyone noticing you. This is considered revelation. Likewise, legislative revelation does not come openly; rather, it comes in secret between Allah the Exalted and His Messenger (ﷺ).

Revelation differs according to the one who reveals, the one to whom it is revealed, and what is revealed.

Allah the Exalted reveals to inanimate things, as He revealed to the earth: ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 5].

And He reveals to the bee: ﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee, "Take for yourself from the mountains, houses..."﴾ [al-Nahl: 68].

And humans other than messengers are inspired: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Nurse him"﴾ [al-Qasas: 7], and He inspired the disciples (al-Hawariyyun).

As for legislative revelation, which concerns obligations, it is a revelation from Allah and an address to the messengers with a method that they convey on behalf of Allah. It is not merely a passing thought or inspiration like the earlier kind. Among revelation is also that the devils inspire their allies. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you; and if you obey them, indeed you would be associators [with Allah]﴾ [al-An'am: 121].

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you from the Book﴾ [Fatir: 31], i.e., from the Qur'an, or from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). ﴿is the truth﴾ [Fatir: 31], i.e., the Qur'an is the very essence of truth. We have known from our grammatical studies that the subject (al-mubtada') always comes definite (ma'rifah), because you are going to pass judgment on it, and you cannot pass judgment on something unknown; you say, for example, "Zayd is diligent" (Zaydun mujtahid). Zayd is known to you, and you have passed judgment on him as being diligent. Thus the unknown is the predicate (al-khabar), which therefore always comes indefinite (nakirah). But if you say "Zayd is the diligent one" (Zaydun huwa al-mujtahid), this means that he has reached such a degree of diligence that whenever diligence is mentioned without qualification, it refers only to him.

Likewise in His saying ﴿is the truth﴾ [Fatir: 31]: the truth does not refer to anything except Him, and He is the very essence of truth. The meaning of truth (al-haqq) is the established thing that does not change or contradict itself. And lest anyone understand that since the Qur'an is the truth, the earlier books are false, He said: ﴿confirming that which is before it﴾ [Fatir: 31]. The Qur'an is true and confirms what preceded it of the heavenly scriptures, so those are also true, because the Qur'an attested to them and did not come in opposition to them.

In another place, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and a guardian over it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, grants the Qur'an the standing of the final seal in human completion. If a ruling came in the earlier books and then a different ruling was sent down in the Qur'an, we take the last ruling, because it abrogated the first for a benefit required by the age and by the nature of obligations, which are graduated according to the conditions of nations.

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, distinguished His Messenger (ﷺ) with a feature not granted to other messengers: earlier messengers conveyed to their peoples what was revealed to them, but Allah permitted His Messenger to convey on behalf of Allah and entrusted him to legislate for his people. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7].

This verse refutes those who say that one should take the Qur'an without the Sunnah, that old-new slander which we hear from time to time from those who proclaim it, and they do not know that the text of the Qur'an obliges them to the Sunnah, to respect it and to act upon it, because it clarifies the Qur'an, explains it, and elaborates what is general in it. Otherwise, what would they say about His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7]?

If I said to you: Is there an article in our constitution stipulating the dismissal of an employee who is absent from his work for fifteen days? There is no such article in the constitution; rather, it is a law laid down by a group of specialists delegated for that purpose, just as a committee is formed for government employees and workers to set laws for them by delegation. Likewise, the Messenger of Allah was delegated by his Lord, mighty and majestic, to legislate for his community and to clarify it for them.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ [Fatir: 31]. Al-Khabir (the Acquainted) is He who knows the hidden aspects of all things as they truly are, and al-Basir (the Seeing) is He from whom nothing is absent, and not an atom's weight escapes Him. You may know a thing without seeing it, and the Truth, glory be to Him, often combines al-Khabir with al-Basir in the Qur'an, as in this verse, or combines al-Latif (the Subtle) with al-Khabir, because acquaintance requires sight and requires subtlety. Al-Latif, as we have said, is He who penetrates things, and nothing prevents Him.

Thus we have said: the most violent of things in their destruction are the minute, subtle ones that are not seen with the naked eye. We used to call them (in the past) microbes, and now the virus has appeared; I think it is more subtle and finer than the microbe, and more violent in its destruction.

We have clarified this matter with the example of one who builds a house and wants to guard against harmful animals and insects, so he places an iron mesh, for instance, over the windows. But this mesh must be suited to the fineness of the thing one fears: what stops wolves is not what stops mice, and what stops mice is not what stops flies and mosquitoes, and so on.

Thus: the finer a thing is, the more violent it is and the more precaution it requires, because it penetrates into the narrowest place and reaches you without your feeling it.

From His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ [Fatir: 31], we understand that Allah alone is capable of legislating for His servants what suits them in every time and place. Therefore the heavenly books multiplied when the diseases differed; and when the world came together and became connected, the Qur'an came as a guardian over all these books.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants...﴾.

The Book is the Qur'an. So this inheritance came after the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and it is evidence that the stage after the Messenger is a stage of inheriting the Book and the method. The scholars inherit it from the Messenger of Allah. That is why there is the hadith: "The scholars are the heirs of the Prophets. The Prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams; they left behind only knowledge, so whoever takes it takes a full share."

While the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was alive, he was the one who conveyed and taught. After his death, Allah entrusted this task to the scholars. The phrase ﴿We caused to inherit﴾ [Fatir: 32] means: We asked them to deal with it as an heir deals with wealth, because the heir of wealth directs it toward the general benefit, and this is also the direction of the message.

Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. So we are the heirs of Muhammad, and whoever among us knows a ruling must convey it. The Messenger is a witness over those to whom he conveyed, and likewise his community will be witnesses over the people to whom they convey.

The phrase ﴿We chose﴾ means: We selected and preferred them over the rest of the community. Then the Exalted divides these people into three categories: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32], who has wronged himself by falling short in the right of this Book that he inherited, so he did not act upon it as he should, and may even commit a major sin, and we seek refuge in Allah.

This category has wronged itself because it has deprived itself of reward. Every obligation that asks you for little effort and gives you abundant reward in return: when you fall short in the little effort, you are without doubt wronging yourself.

﴿And among them is one who is moderate﴾ means: he acts upon it at some times, mixing a righteous deed with a bad one.

﴿And among them is one foremost in good deeds, by Allah's permission﴾.

May Allah make us among them, if Allah wills. The word (sabiq, foremost) indicates that there is a race and competition: whichever of the racers reaches the goal set for the race first, and the people of this category compete in good deeds.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿We chose﴾ shows that the word of monotheism has a price, belief in the Messenger of Allah has a price, and acting upon what the Messenger of Allah brought has a price. Even if among these chosen ones there is one who wrongs himself by falling short, and even by committing sins, he is still among the chosen, because he said "There is no god but Allah," and the Exalted does not equate one who says this word with one who denies it. "There is no god but Allah is My fortress; whoever says it enters My fortress."

Therefore the Exalted mentioned for these believers who inherited the Book two attributes: ﴿those whom We have chosen from Our servants﴾, so He described them with being chosen and with servanthood to Him, the Exalted.

So: the Book was revealed to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and his community inherited the Book after him, so it is an extension of his message. That is why Allah entrusted this community to carry His method to all people until the Hour arises, while He did not entrust others.

The Exalted has undertaken to preserve this Book and did not leave its preservation to anyone, as happened with the books before the Qur'an...

If you say: How can one who wrongs himself be among the chosen, when he commits sins and perhaps major sins? We say: as soon as the servant says, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," he is chosen. Allah has chosen him over the disbelievers by this word, even if sin occurs from him afterward.

When the Exalted mentions a sin, declares it forbidden and prescribes a punishment for it, this is a permission that it will occur. For example, Allah forbade theft and prescribed a hadd for it, and forbade adultery and prescribed a hadd for it, as if such things happen in the Muslim society. As for lying, for example, He did not prescribe a hadd or a punishment for it...

So the believer is expected to commit adultery and theft, but is not expected to lie, for it is the attribute furthest from the believer. Why? They said: because lying contradicts reality and reverses facts, and the believer does not lie, since he utters "There is no god but Allah." If he is a liar, how do I know he was truthful in this word? So lying demolishes faith from its foundation. Therefore Allah did not prescribe a punishment for it, because it is not conceivable from a believer.

The moderate one is the one whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, who mixed a righteous deed with a bad one. In another place the Exalted says about this category:

﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another bad. Perhaps Allah will accept their repentance; indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Tawbah: 102]...

﴿That is the great bounty.﴾ Yes, the Exalted deals with us with great bounty, and gives us examples to make us love the religion. A good deed with Him is multiplied tenfold, or increased to seven hundred times and to many multiples, and a bad deed is recompensed with its like.

Whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds is hoped to enter Paradise. Whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds is left to the command of Allah: if He wills, He punishes him in justice, and his end is Paradise; and if He wills, He forgives him by His bounty. If he hastens to sincere repentance and is sincere, Allah replaces his bad deeds with good deeds...

Our Lord deals with us by bounty, as evidenced by the fact that He admitted the one who wronged himself, and admitted the moderate one into the company of His chosen servants.

Then the Exalted explains to us this great bounty, saying:

﴿Gardens of Eden, which they will enter; they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 33:

You will notice that ﴿Jannāt﴾ [Fāṭir: 33] is plural, meaning many gardens, not one garden. And "Jannāt ʿAdn" (the Gardens of Eden) means a permanent dwelling that never ends. The gardens are described here as lasting because Adam, peace be upon him, had previously been admitted to the Garden but then left it. As for the Garden of the Hereafter, it is lasting and everlasting; no one who enters it leaves it.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾ [Fāṭir: 33]. You will notice that the Real, glory be to Him, mentions adornment and ornament here before the necessities, which means that the necessities are already provided and settled. This adornment in the Hereafter will be of gold and of silk, and these are forbidden to men in this world, but in the Hereafter it is a different matter.

The word (asāwir) is the plural of (aswira), and (aswira) is the plural of (siwār), like (fu'ād) and (af'ida). It is a plural of a plural to indicate abundance, and that you will be adorned, God willing, in the Garden with many bracelets filling the arm from the wrist to the upper arm.
