It is well known that the siwār (bracelet) is what is worn on the wrist and what women wear for adornment in this world, each according to her means, to the point that some wealthy women wear a wide bracelet on the upper arm which they call (dumluk), out of the abundance of their wealth.

It is strange that some men hasten to the adornment of the Garden, but by other than its path, so they wear bracelets, which is what is now called (al-insiyāl).

The Real, glory be to Him, mentioned gold bracelets in the adornment because kings in ancient times used to wear them and adorn themselves with them. Khosrow had two bracelets, which have a story in our history. When Suraqa ibn Mālik embraced Islam, he was lean, and his forearms resembled the forearms of a goat, and some of the Companions would mock him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from that and said a saying whose meaning they came to understand later. He said: "How will you be with them, meaning Suraqa's forearms, in the bracelets of Khosrow?"

When the Muslims conquered the lands of Persia and seized the palaces and wealth of Khosrow, the two bracelets fell to Suraqa's share at the distribution of the spoils. When ʿUmar saw them on his arms, he said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke the truth."

As for these bracelets ﴿of gold and pearls﴾ [Fāṭir: 33]: gold is known to come from the mountains, and pearls are an ornament of the sea.

Consider the precision of the Qur'anic expression here: when it spoke of the bracelets it used a plural of a plural to indicate abundance, but when it spoke of garments it said ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾ [Fāṭir: 33] in the singular. Why? They said: because you need many garments only to ward off cold or heat from yourself, and there is none of this in the Garden.

This is the words of the believers at the moment they enjoy the bliss of Paradise. They do not forget the Bestower, glory be to Him, so they praise Him first for having legislated for them the methodology (manhaj) that brought them to this bliss, and they praise Him for having saved them and rescued them from disbelief and guided them to faith. So this is a compound praise.

The phrase "al-hamdu lillah" (All praise is due to Allah) is the last thing that those who are blessed will say in the Hereafter, as the Exalted said: ﴿And the last of their prayer will be: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Yunus: 10].

And from Allah's kindness to His servants and His tenderness toward them, He teaches them how to praise Him, glory be to Him, and teaches them this concise phrase made up of a subject and predicate: al-hamdu lillah. This is because people differ in their ability to perform eloquent expression and articulate speech: one person is eloquent and able to compose beautiful style and embellish phrases, while another is not skilled in any of this. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, taught us how to praise Him with a simple, easy expression in which everyone is equal.

For this reason it has come in the supplication of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to his Lord: "...I cannot enumerate praise upon You; You are as You have praised Yourself." We have said that the phrase (al-hamdu lillah) requires an endless chain of praise: when you say over a blessing, "al-hamdu lillah," this phrase itself is a blessing that requires praise and deserves praise, and thus the Real, glory be to Him, remains praised, and the servant remains praising without end.

His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿Who has removed from us the grief﴾ is a third blessing deserving praise. So the praise is first for the blessings, second for your having praised Allah for His blessings, and third you praise Allah who has removed from you the grief. Grief (hazan) is everything that saddens or distresses you, or it is the persistence of sorrow in a person.

A person enjoys bliss in this world and is pleased by it, but fear of its loss spoils it for him, so he lives worried and sorrowful, fearing that the blessing will escape him or that he will escape it through death. As for the Hereafter, a person does not think of any of this at all, for this thought has gone with the passing of this world, and the reward in the Hereafter is lasting and enduring; it will not escape you, nor will you escape it.

As for their saying, ﴿Indeed our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾, it is as though they accuse themselves of shortcoming, that they did not fulfill the right of Allah as it should be fulfilled, and that what they are in of bliss is only because their Lord is Forgiving, who overlooks their shortcomings, and Appreciative, who thanks them for righteous deeds after He enabled them to do them and helped them to them.

The meaning of ﴿who has settled us﴾ [Fatir: 35]: He has admitted us and made it our abode. ﴿in the abode of permanence﴾ [Fatir: 35]: meaning lasting residence, and what is intended is Paradise. Paradise is the abode of lasting residence, whereas this world is nothing but a passage to the Hereafter and is not called a dwelling of permanence. Allah has made this Paradise their abode not because of their deeds, but by His grace and generosity. Even if you have a righteous deed, it goes back to Allah's legislating it for you. So everything returns to the grace of Allah.

As for their saying ﴿no fatigue touches us therein﴾ [Fatir: 35], meaning in Paradise, ﴿nor does weariness touch us therein﴾ [Fatir: 35]: nasab means toil and hardship, and lughub means exhaustion and lassitude that result from fatigue, such as from the movements of the body's faculties. In our striving in this world, a person is exposed to many hardships, to the extent that we say "yadrib fi al-ard" (he strikes the earth), meaning he strives. It is thus an exhausting, laborious process, from which a person returns weary and worn out. This is lughub, until you rest from it and recover, and your strength and vigour return to you for work once more.

From this same meaning is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us﴾ [Qaf: 38].

Some have said: nasab is the fatigue of the limbs, and lughub is the fatigue of the hearts, meaning the anxiety that occupies a person's mind.

On this meaning Shawqi, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

*What the back can bear is not a burden;*
*the burden is only what the chest holds.*

When Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the most severe of Allah's soldiers on earth, he said: "Worry." If it takes hold of a person, it troubles him and disturbs his sleep. Therefore they said: "Worry overcomes sleep," and it is more severe than that. Worry never ceases to act upon a person until he becomes lean after being stout, as al-Mutanabbi said:

*Worry seizes the robust and makes him thin,*
*and whitens the forelock of the youth and makes him old.*

After the Exalted Lord has told us about the believers, His chosen servants, and about their reward in the Gardens of Eden, so that the soul may rejoice and open itself to the glad tidings for the righteous, He mentions what stands opposite to that: the warnings for the foolish. Mentioning the opposite increases the meaning's clarity, and this is a feature of the Qur'anic style, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in the Hellfire﴾ [Al-Infitar: 13-14].

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So let them laugh a little and weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn﴾ [At-Tawbah: 82].

Likewise, here, He says, glorified is He:

﴿And those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell; it will not be decreed upon them...﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 36:

The lam in ﴿لَهُمْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ ["For them is the Fire of Hell"] indicates possession and specific belonging, as when we say: "So-and-so has such-and-such." It is as if they are attached to it, and it is attached to them with the attachment of an owner to what he owns. And at the moment they enter it, God forbid, they wish to be freed from it, even by death, in line with the saying of the poet:

"It is enough of a disease for you that you see death as a cure,
and it is enough of the fates that they should be mere wishes."

Yes: they wish for release, even through death, but far from them is that. This meaning is clear in His saying, exalted is He, in another place: ﴿وَنَادَوْاْ يٰمَالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ مَّاكِثُونَ﴾ ["They will call, 'O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!' He will say, 'Indeed, you will remain.'" (43:77)] So death is not a punishment; rather, for them it is a relief from a greater and more lasting punishment.

I recall that some of the advocates [of modernist views] claimed that the Book of God contains no evidence for stoning the married adulteress, and he based this on His saying, exalted is He, concerning slave women: ﴿فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى ٱلْمُحْصَنَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾ ["Upon them is half the punishment of free married women" (4:25)].

On the basis that stoning cannot be divided, so that there could be a half-stoning, and since stoning cannot be divided, there is no stoning at all. Our Lord, glory be to Him, inspired us, and we say, praise be to God: first we must define what "punishment" ('adhab) is. Punishment is the infliction of pain upon a living being. When we gather the verses of the Qur'an on the subject together, the picture becomes clear and the meaning appears. God says in the story of Solomon's hoopoe, peace be upon him: ﴿لأُعَذِّبَنَّهُ عَذَاباً شَدِيداً أَوْ لأَاْذبَحَنَّهُ﴾ ["I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or surely slaughter him" (27:21)]. Thus: death, slaughter, or killing is not a punishment. And stoning is a causing of death, and causing death is the ending of punishment.

When the Almighty, exalted is He, revealed this text, He willed that His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, should have an explanation of this text. There is a difference between a ruling you take from the text and a ruling you take from the actual practice of the Lawgiver, may God bless him and grant him peace, because a text may be interpreted by you, whereas actual practice by the Messenger of God admits of no interpretation. It is established that the Messenger of God did in fact stone.

Had the matter been as the advocate claims, the verse would read "upon them is half of what is upon the married women," without mentioning the punishment. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾ ["of the punishment"] means: not of anything else. It is thus an explanation of the half: half the punishment. Stoning is not a punishment; rather it is an ending of punishment.

Then He, glory be to Him, informs about the state of the people of the Fire: ﴿وَلاَ يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمْ مِّنْ عَذَابِهَا﴾ ["Nor will its punishment be lightened for them" (35:36)], meaning: it is a constant punishment that does not cease or slacken. A person in this world, for example, may be afflicted, God forbid, by being detained and beaten, so that he confesses to what happened, until his body becomes numb (atrash), meaning he feels no pain from the many blows; therefore such a person is struck with one lash, or several lashes, and then feels nothing afterwards, and the saying of the poet applies to him:

"Whoever is humiliated, humiliation becomes easy for him;
a dead wound feels no pain."

Or the saying of another:

"And whenever arrows struck me,
the arrowheads broke against arrowheads."

So the punishment of this world may be lightened, even by this bad habit, which is the loss of sensation when the skin loses its connection to the brain. But the punishment of the Hereafter is not lightened for them, however long it lasts; therefore He, exalted is He, says in another place: ﴿كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بَدَّلْنَٰهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَهَا لِيَذُوقُواْ ٱلْعَذَابَ﴾ ["Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment" (4:56)].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 37:

The meaning of ﴿yaṣṭariḫūn﴾ [Fāṭir: 37] is: they cry out and shout, seeking help and asking for rescue. Al-ṣurākh (crying out) is a plea for someone who will deliver you from hardship, distress or punishment. We hear this kind of sound, for example, when a fire breaks out, God forbid, and people cry out seeking help.

These people cry out ﴿fīhā﴾ [Fāṭir: 37], that is, in the Fire, saying in their outcry: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do﴾ [Fāṭir: 37]. First: it is strange of them to say now "Our Lord" (rabbanā), this word which they denied in the world and disbelieved in; now they utter it, but after its time has passed. Then they acknowledge against themselves that their deeds in the world were not righteous, and this is a consideration that counts against them, not for them, and it increases their punishment rather than lightening it for them.

Then, even if God were to answer them, and far is that from them, would they actually do righteousness as they claim? God has known their lie, and He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'ām: 28].

So this is merely speech in time of distress; if they returned, they would revert to what they were upon. Therefore God answers them: ﴿Did We not give you lives long enough that whoever would be mindful might be mindful therein..﴾ [Fāṭir: 37], meaning: We gave you enough life in the world to suffice for remembrance and reflection for whoever wished to remember or take heed.

﴿And there came to you the warner﴾ [Fāṭir: 37], the Messenger who warned you and cautioned you about the consequence of your deeds, and yet you did not return to the right path, nor did you examine yourselves until the time had passed.

﴿So taste; for the wrongdoers there is no helper﴾ [Fāṭir: 37]. That is: taste the punishment. The meaning of ﴿nāṣir﴾ [Fāṭir: 37] is one who gives aid. The naṣīr (helper) is the one who defends you with strength and enters the battle with you, whereas in another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿no protecting friend (walī) nor helper (naṣīr)﴾ [al-Shūrā: 31]. The walī (protecting friend) is the close relative who defends you through entreaty, appeal and tender affection; these people have neither a walī nor a naṣīr in this situation.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Indeed, God is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens...﴾.

This verse came as a justification for what precedes it. Allah, the Exalted, knows all that is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and He knows the secrets of the breasts, their inner thoughts, their intentions, and whatever clings to them. Allah, glorified is He, knew the intentions of the people of the Fire, and He knew that if they were returned to the world they would go back to what they had been doing. This is an experiment that will not be repeated. Therefore Allah concluded this situation with them and decreed that they would not be returned.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth. So whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief...﴾.

Meaning of ﴿khalā'if﴾ [Fāṭir: 39]: successors (khulafā'), one of you succeeding another. In another verse, ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khalīfah (vicegerent)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], meaning a vicegerent of Allah on His earth. Therefore Allah has bestowed upon us attributes from His own attributes, so that we may carry out our task on earth. If we find in ourselves the power to act, it is from the power of Allah; if we find wisdom in our conduct, it is an outpouring of the wisdom of Allah; and if we find in ourselves honour, it is from the honour of Allah... etc.

This is the meaning of khilāfah (vicegerency), because when a person reflects upon his own self, he finds that everything in him is bestowed upon him by his Creator, glorified is He, and is not intrinsic to him.

We have said before, for example: when you merely intend to rise from your place, you find yourself standing without knowing what happened in your organs and muscles, or how the commands were issued to these muscles to move. This is in reality one of the attributes of the Creator, glorified is He, which He has bestowed upon you a portion of. The proof is that if He, glorified is He, removes this power from you, you cannot stand; and He has indeed removed it from others, to show you that your strength is not intrinsic to you, so do not be deceived by it.

You observe, for example, that after the development of industry, scientists used human movements in the manufacture of (cranes and bulldozers). You see that a single movement requires several movements of the machine, and requires the driver to press a certain button for that movement. As for you, you need nothing of this in the movement of your limbs.

By merely wanting an action, you perform it, and your organs and muscles respond to you and carry out what you want from them, without you feeling anything. So if you, being a creature of Allah, when you want something to do it without commanding any of your organs or any muscle of your body, then what of the Creator, glorified is He?

Do you deny that He, glorified is He, says to a thing "Be," and it is? ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 82].

When you want a movement, you do not command any of your organs, because you do not know which of them to command. The organs, muscles and nerves are intertwined things, and you do not know what is going on within you to perform this movement. Therefore the Creator, glorified is He, fashioned you in a form whereby your organs respond to you merely by your will. As for the Creator, glorified is He, He commands things and says to them: "Be." Because He, glorified is He, knows the mechanism that moves.

Also, the Creator, glorified is He, has not left you in command of your limbs; rather He made them subservient to you and subdued them to your will, because you cannot guarantee, if you command them, that they will obey you and respond to you. As for the Creator, glorified is He, when He commands things, they obey Him. The proof is that when a person is deprived of the ability to move, or when this illness befalls him—we seek refuge in Allah—he wants to move one of his fingers and cannot.

And the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, before summoning the vicegerent into existence, created for him before creating him, guaranteed for him his sustenance and the necessities of his life until the Hour, then left the intellects to work and to derive from the necessities what refines and enriches life.

So: you, O vicegerent of Allah on earth, are not to receive the command of Allah in "do this" and "do not do that" with obedience and submission. So if you disbelieve after that, ﴿whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾ [Fāṭir: 39]—you have disbelieved, meaning you did not obey "do" and "do not." And kufr (disbelief) means concealment; to disbelieve in Allah means to conceal Him, as though Allah were manifest and the disbeliever concealed Him by his disbelief. Therefore we have said: disbelief is the first proof of faith, for were it not for the existence of Allah, there would be no disbelief.

Just as there is disbelief in Allah who made you His successor, there is disbelief in that over which you have been made successor: disbelief in the blessing, by forgetting its Giver and the One who bestowed it upon you. Among the disbelief in blessings is laziness in deriving and extracting them from the depths of the earth, leaving them buried so that people do not benefit from them. Among the disbelief in blessings also is not paying Allah's right in them, and concealing them from those who deserve them and need them.

What the world now suffers of crises in food and famines is nothing but the natural result of disbelief in blessings, either through idleness and sitting back from extracting them, or that we extract them but our souls are miserly and stingy with them. This is proven by the fact that we lived a long period in the narrow valley, and did not try, and did not try to extract the bounties of the desert. When we became aware of the necessity of invading the desert and cultivating it, we were afflicted with a craze for extraction, so we planted luxuries and did not plant necessities. You find the market full of oranges, bananas, grapes, cantaloupe, strawberries, etc., while we (beg for) a loaf of bread and solicit others for the necessities of our lives.

So: the recompense here is of the same kind as the deed: ﴿whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾ [Fāṭir: 39], meaning he is repaid for it. Whoever disbelieves in the Benefactor has his recompense, and his recompense is punishment in the Hereafter; and whoever disbelieves in the blessing has his recompense, and his recompense is that he dies of hunger and is humiliated before others. If he is humbled before others, he will not carry out any command or prohibition, and will not care about any religion or methodology.

May Allah have mercy on our forefathers who said: "Whose bread comes from his own axe, his head bows to no one."

Then He, glorified is He, says, explaining the consequence of disbelief: ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers increases them in nothing with their Lord except hatred, and the disbelief of the disbelievers increases them in nothing but loss﴾ [Fāṭir: 39]. Yes, disbelief increases its possessor in hatred and aversion from Allah, Mighty and Majestic; for with whom did you disbelieve? You disbelieved in Allah, your Lord, your Creator, your Provider, and the Giver of blessings to you. Every disbelief in any of these entails for you aversion and hatred from Allah, and this hatred increases with persistence in disbelief and insistence upon it. Then after all this, disbelief increases its possessor in ﴿loss﴾ [Fāṭir: 39]. And what loss is greater than disbelief in Allah? The loss here is great, because it is ruin and forfeiture of the good of both this world and the Hereafter.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 40:

The address in "Say" (qul) is to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Tell Me about your partners whom you invoke besides Allah﴾ [Fatir: 40], meaning: inform me about them. It is not merely a question about seeing, as when I say to you: "Did you see so-and-so yesterday?" and you answer "yes" or "no." Here the intent is to report on their condition, and to ask them to inform about the condition of their partners whom they worshipped besides Allah, making them themselves the judges in this matter.

﴿Show me what they have created from the earth﴾ [Fatir: 40], meaning: inform me whether they alone have done any creating. ﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ [Fatir: 40], meaning: did they share the creation with Me, with their hands working alongside Mine in creating? ﴿Or have We given them a Book so that they stand upon clear evidence from it?﴾ [Fatir: 40], a Book permitting them to associate others with Allah and serving as a proof for their polytheism.

The Exalted and Glorified explains this matter elsewhere, saying: ﴿I did not make them witnesses to the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor to their own creation, and I would never take misleaders as helpers﴾ [al-Kahf: 51].

So the Exalted does not merely deny their sharing with Him in creation; He denies even that they witnessed this matter. They have no knowledge of creation and no connection to it, and they cannot tell how the heavens and the earth were created, nor how they themselves were created.

Then He says: ﴿Rather﴾ [Fatir: 40], where "rather" (bal) is a turning away from the preceding speech and an affirmation of the ruling after it: ﴿the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾ [Fatir: 40]. Here "in" (in) carries the meaning of the negative "ma," meaning: the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion. Delusion (ghurur) is the deception that clothes falsehood in the garb of truth in order to attract, and adorns it for them so as to deceive them with it.

From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O human being, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Most Generous?﴾ [al-Infitar: 6], meaning: what has enticed you to disobey Him, and what has encouraged you to defy His commands? It is as if the Exalted teaches us the answer through His words "the Most Generous," for what deceived us about Allah is His generosity and bounty.

The meaning, then, is: rather, all of this is falsehood. Their partners created nothing, did not share in the creation of anything, and We did not give them a Book that could serve as a proof for them. All of this is deception and embellishment on their part, and the reality is that they delude one another and deceive one another with these falsehoods.

Then the Exalted says:

﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease...﴾.

And the verse concludes with His saying, may He be exalted: "Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving." But you may ask: what is the connection between these two attributes of Allah, the Forbearing (al-Halim) and the Forgiving (al-Ghafur), and the matter of the holding back of the heavens and the earth, which is a cosmic matter?

They said: because this matter attracts much argument, and a person often oversteps his limits concerning it, so he asks about what he should not delve into, and about the manner in which the heavens and the earth are held up, while he walks across the regions of the earth and rides the airplane through the air of the sky, yet he sees nothing and sees no pillars.

This is a matter in which we have no say, and it is sufficient that the Creator, mighty and majestic, has informed us about it by His saying: "He created the heavens without pillars that you can see" [Luqman: 10]. That is, either there are in fact no pillars for them, or they have pillars but you do not see them; both meanings are valid, and we must stop at this limit.

So the Truth, glorified is He, is Forbearing: He does not punish those who are bold toward Him, those who delve into His right (in His regard), rather even those who deny His existence, He does not hasten to punish them. And had it not been for His forbearance, He would have dropped them upon their heads...

So then: had it not been for Allah's forbearance toward us and His forgiveness of our sins, the heavens and the earth would not be held up, and this universe would collapse upon whoever is in it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 35, verse 42:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿jahda aymanihim﴾ [Fatir: 42]. That is: they strove in swearing and taking oaths with the most emphatic oaths. ﴿La-in jaa'ahum nadhir﴾ [Fatir: 42], a messenger, ﴿la-yakununna ahda﴾ [Fatir: 42], more rightly guided, ﴿min ihda al-umam﴾ [Fatir: 42], that is, more guided than the previous nations. Meaning: they would be in the forefront.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies this meaning in another place, where He says, glory be to Him: ﴿And indeed they used to say, "If only we had a reminder from the former peoples, we would have been sincere servants of Allah."﴾ [al-Saffat: 167-169].

All of this is their saying with their mouths, and Allah knows that they are liars. Yet He, glory be to Him, gives them free rein and does not expose this lie, saying to them: Leave aside the former peoples; here is the Reminder you asked for, and you said that by it you would become the most rightly guided of people. The intended meaning here is the message of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿But when a warner came to them, it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ [Fatir: 42]. That is: turning away and distancing from the truth and from guidance. Why? Because the Reminder that came to them came through Muhammad. Had it come through a great man, as they say, they would have accepted it: ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from one of the two cities?"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31]. So Allah answers them: ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32].

It is strange of them that they would want to divide the mercy of Allah according to their own desires and the choosing of the Messenger of Allah as they like: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

How could it be otherwise, when Allah has already distributed among them the simplest matters of their worldly life, making this one rich and that one poor, this one strong and that one weak?

Yet this statement of theirs is evidence that the Qur'an, in their eyes, is beyond reproach, and that they do not deny it, even though they called it sorcery, soothsaying, and poetry. Despite this, they acknowledge that the Qur'an is beyond reproach; but its flaw, in their view, is that it was sent down upon Muhammad specifically.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, explains the cause of their aversion, saying:

﴿arrogance in the land and evil plotting; but the evil plotting does not encompass...﴾ [Fatir: 43].

Yes, they were arrogant toward the truth and did not accept it. Why? Because this truth came to bring them down from the lofty position of lordship to a servitude that is proposed and stripped of dignity among all creatures. They had grown accustomed to lordship, and equality weighs heavily on them, and they would have to be, they and their slaves, like the teeth of a comb.

It is as if Allah, glorified is He, were answering them: O you who are arrogant toward accepting the truth by virtue of the lordship you possess, should it not have befitted you to be ashamed for your honour, and to ask yourselves: from where did you get this lordship?

By Allah, if Allah Most High had enabled Abraha to demolish the Ka'bah in the incident of the Elephant, and people had turned to another Ka'bah in Sana'a, would you have had lordship? Would you have had awe or renown among people? Then: you should have used your minds, and considered where this awe came from, and where these provisions that are driven to you come from. You used to forbid people from circumambulating the House except naked, so that they would buy clothes from you.

And read the words of Allah: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plot into misguidance? And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and He made them like eaten straw.﴾ [al-Fil: 1-5].

Why did Allah do this to the companions of the elephant? The Almighty answers in the following surah: ﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh — their accustomed security in the caravans of winter and summer. So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.﴾ [Quraysh: 1-4].

That is: I did not do this to the companions of the elephant except for the sake of Quraysh, to preserve their lordship and to provide them with sustenance and security. Yet despite all this, they were arrogant toward My method, they confronted My Messenger, opposed him and plotted against him.

﴿Arrogance in the land and evil scheming﴾ [Fatir: 43], i.e., against the Messenger of Allah and those who believed with him, to turn them away from their religion. Had they known the reason for their arrogance, this arrogance would have guided them to faith in Him who made them nobles.

Then the Almighty establishes this reality: ﴿And the evil scheming does not encompass except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43]. They schemed against the Messenger of Allah, plotted against him, conspired against him, harmed the believers in him and tortured them. But Allah made their scheme recoil upon their own necks, as He said in another place: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you — they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of planners﴾ [al-Anfal: 30], i.e., to imprison you.

They devised every kind of stratagem to eliminate the call of Islam, and none of them succeeded. They even plotted to kill the Prophet (ﷺ), but Allah frustrated their endeavour, and the Messenger of Allah went out from among them while they were asleep, sprinkling dust upon their heads. Then, when they despaired of eliminating him through trickery, they turned to the jinn and sought their help to bewitch the Messenger of Allah, but Allah saved him from them. Then they tried to put poison into his food (ﷺ).

It is as if Allah, Most High, says to them: Spare your efforts, for you will not extinguish the light of Allah, nor will you turn Muhammad away from his call, neither by mockery and ridicule, nor by harm, scheming and plotting by night, nor even by sorcery.

The meaning of ﴿And the evil scheming does not encompass except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43] is: it descends upon them, surrounds them, and turns back upon them.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then do they await anything but the precedent of the former peoples?﴾ [Fatir: 43]. That is: they await nothing but the sunnah (precedent) of the earlier ones concerning the earlier messengers. The sunnah is the established and customary way and practice. Did they find, among the earlier messengers and earlier nations, that Allah sent a messenger and then forsook him or abandoned him, and did not destroy his enemies and those who denied him? The support of the messengers is a established practice, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers — they will be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173].

Then Allah, glorified is He, affirms this meaning, saying: ﴿And you will not find any alteration in the sunnah of Allah﴾ [Fatir: 43]. Why does the sunnah of Allah not change or transform? Because Allah, Most High, first has no *bada'* (a change of mind arising from new knowledge), and the meaning of *bada'* is that you do something, then it occurs to you that you should do something better than it. And also because He, glorified is He, is one God, having no second and no partner, so no one can correct Him or alter His action.

Then Allah, the Most High, says:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them, and they were greater in...﴾.

The interrogative in "أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُواْ فِي الأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ" (Have they not travelled through the earth and looked…) expresses astonishment, meaning: how can this come from them? "Have they not travelled through the earth and looked at how was the end of those before them?" — that is, of the deniers whom God seized — "and they were stronger than them in power."

As He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and by night. Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138].

Yes, in the movement of their lives and in their journeys they passed by the dwellings of ʿAd and Thamud, the people of Lot and the people of Salih, etc. They saw their traces and what destruction and ruin befell them after they denied their messengers. They were people of civilisations, buildings and palaces unmatched… And strange it is that the people of these civilisations, whose fame filled the horizons, could not devise for their civilisations anything to preserve them from perishing.

We have an observation regarding His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُواْ فِي الأَرْضِ﴾ (Have they not travelled through the earth).

For a short time ago we used to believe that "travelling in the earth" means over the earth, since we walk on it, not in it, until we discovered that the earth contains the sustenance, and the lord of sustenance is air. The evidence: you can endure without water for several days, and endure longer than that without food, but you cannot endure without air beyond a single inhalation or exhalation; if it were withheld from you, you would part from life.

We came to know that the air of the earth is from the earth; therefore it revolves with it and is bound to it. So in this sense we do not walk on the earth; rather we walk in it. Even one who flies by aircraft in the upper layers of the atmosphere is also travelling in the earth, because the air is from the earth, and it is the origin of its sustenance in breath and food…

In this verse, ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُواْ فِي الأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ﴾, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants from the unbelievers that they look at the places of life, not at our words nor at their words, but at the observed reality of life. So He said "أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُواْ" because they had indeed travelled; they were a people who had trade, in summer to the north and in winter to the south.

In these journeys they saw many traces of those who came before them. Did they see among the earlier ones a messenger who was defeated by the deniers of him? Rather, God defeated the deniers and the unbelievers, and decreed victory for the true believers. And those whom God seized were stronger than them, but the power of mankind, however far its progress, what can it do before the power of God? So do not look at the power of the messenger; look at the power of the one who sent him and who undertook to preserve and support him.

Thus: this is a battle not between creation and creation, but between creatures opposing the Creator, glorified is He. So do you think you can frustrate God? Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, negates that they could be "muʿjizīn" (those who frustrate Him) and negates that they could be "muʿājizīn" (those who contend to frustrate Him). There is a difference between the two: "muʿjiz" (one who frustrates) means if he frustrates Him even once, i.e., brings about what defeats Him; whereas "muʿājiz" carries participation and mutual action, as if the frustration were a back-and-forth contest, with taking and returning.

So it is as if the Truth, glorified is He, gives them respite and delays them, granting them dominance in some rounds, in order to exhaust every kind of trick and all their strength. Thus: however great your strength, and however much you seek help and strengthen yourselves with other civilisations, you will never frustrate God, for God, exalted is He, is not frustrated by anything, and He has no partner or counterpart that could help you. He is one God who helps and supports those who believe in Him, while you have no helper. And the Truth, glorified is He, destroyed the deniers before you, who were stronger than you, and whoever is able to overcome the stronger is all the more able to overcome the weaker.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wishes to affirm a factual matter, He may bring it in the form of a statement, saying: "They travelled in the earth and saw such and such." But here He turned from the declarative to the interrogative, meaning: ask them, did they travel or not?

The Truth, glorified is He, asks this question only while certain that they will say, "We did travel," and this confirms the statement, since it is an acknowledgement from the addressee himself; just as the interrogative in negative form is stronger in establishing the addressee's assent than the interrogative in affirmative form.

The matter of travelling in the earth has taken wide scope in the Noble Qur'an, because God, exalted is He, wants people to look at the cosmic signs, to reflect upon the cosmos in order to grasp its secrets and the signs of power within it. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, commands us once with His saying: ﴿قُلْ سِيرُواْ فِي الأَرْضِ فَانظُرُواْ﴾ [al-Naml: 69] ("Say: travel in the earth and then look"), and once: ﴿قُلْ سِيرُواْ فِي الأَرْضِ ثُمَّ انْظُرُواْ﴾ [al-Anʿam: 11] ("Say: travel in the earth, then look").

So what is the difference between the two expressions?

They said: travelling in the earth occurs either for looking and taking lessons, or for exploitation. So His saying, exalted is He, ﴿فَانظُرُواْ﴾ [al-Naml: 69], is for travel whose purpose is taking lessons and reflecting upon the signs of God and upon the wondrous architecture of the cosmos that points us to the power of the Creator, glorified is He.

As for His saying ﴿ثُمَّ انْظُرُواْ﴾ [al-Anʿam: 11], it is for travel whose purpose is work, exploitation and seeking provision. So even if you travel through the regions of the earth seeking provision and exploitation, do not forget or neglect reflection and taking lessons, and do not deprive yourself of looking at the signs and at the vast dominion of God, especially when the environments differ…

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِن شَيْءٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَلاَ فِي الأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَلِيماً قَدِيراً﴾ ("And God is not such as to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or in the earth; indeed He is ever Knowing, Competent"). We have already spoken about the meaning of "yuʿjizahu" (frustrate Him). The verse here does not negate that something in the heavens or the earth could frustrate the Truth, glorified is He; rather it negates merely that this be imagined or conceived. This is a matter that is not conceivable and does not occur at all.

His saying "مِن شَيْءٍ" (from anything) here is explicit in generality, meaning: from the very beginning of what is called a "thing," as you say "ma ʿindi māl" (I have no wealth). It is possible that you have some wealth, but it is little and not counted; but if you say "ma ʿindi min māl" (I have none of wealth at all), you have negated the existence of everything that is called wealth, however little, even if it is a single coin.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَلِيماً قَدِيراً﴾ explains the reason why nothing frustrates Him, glorified is He: God, exalted is He, is Knowing with an all-encompassing knowledge from which nothing escapes; if they plot anything, God knows it and knows its place. Then He, glorified is He, is Competent, knowing with power. These two are the elements of dominance: knowledge and power. You know the thing, and you are able to repel it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 35, verse 45 (part 1 of 2):

The Almighty, glory be to Him, is Merciful; He continues His bounties even upon those who disbelieve in Him and disobey His commands. Had Allah taken them to account for their wrongdoing, and their wrongdoing is great, He would not have left a single one of them. Why, then, does Allah deal with us in this manner, and why does He grant us such respite? They said: Because He is our Lord and Creator, and He knows that man is weak before the desires of his soul, weak before his whims and before his devil. Therefore His forbearance precedes His anger, and His pardon precedes His punishment, and He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

It is related in a narration (athar) that the Almighty addresses us saying: "Had you not sinned, I would have created another creation other than you who would sin, then they would seek forgiveness, and I would forgive them." Otherwise, how would the Almighty be described as Oft-Returning (Tawwab) and Much-Forgiving (Ghaffar)? The Almighty wishes to establish for Himself all the attributes of perfection, the first of which is necessary existence (al-wujud al-wajib), then life, and all the attributes follow these two attributes.

These attributes of Allah, the Exalted, may be divided into two categories: a category that has an opposite, which are the attributes of action (sifat al-fi'l) of Allah, such as: the Giver of Life (al-Muhyi), whose opposite is the Causer of Death (al-Mumit), and the Exalter (al-Mu'izz), whose opposite is the Abaser (al-Mudhill); and a category that has no opposite, which are the attributes of essence (sifat al-dhat), such as: the Living (al-Hayy), the Mighty (al-'Aziz), the Subduer (al-Qahhar), the Forbearing (al-Halim); these are attributes that have no contrary.

The Almighty does not take people to account for what they have earned, that is, for transgression and wrongdoing. This is because Allah created man and created for him desires and instincts, and all matters of religion came to elevate these desires and to refine these instincts, not to erase them. They came to refine them, not to eliminate them. Otherwise, had the Almighty wished that these transgressions and this wrongdoing not occur, He would not have placed the instincts in the first place.

For example, the instinct of sexuality, Allah created it for the cultivation of the earth, and Allah wants man to elevate this instinct so that it is within what is lawful and under the canopy of the Shari'ah. We have previously explained the difference in this matter: when it takes place in the light and under the canopy of Allah's law, and in accordance with the words of Allah, and how we rejoice in it, announce it, and take pride in it; whereas if it takes place in secret, far from what Allah has legislated, one seeks to conceal it and to rid oneself of its fruit, if it has any fruit, and if it appears to people, it becomes a stain of shame that cannot be erased.

Therefore it has come in the hadith, i.e., the matter that you used to be jealous of and would not accept, now you rejoice in it and invite people to it. Why? Because it came by the lawful path that Allah has prescribed, and the word of truth is what brought forth the emotions and made the stimulating matter a source of happiness with no reproach in it.

Likewise, the instinct of curiosity exists in man so that he may contemplate the universe around him and seek the secrets of Allah within it, and Allah did not make it for spying on people and tracking their private matters and honour. Likewise, eating and drinking are instincts that Allah placed because they are a foundation of life, and they should remain within these limits, the limits of sustaining life, and not turn into gluttony and voracity, reaching the point of overindulgence.

Allah placed the instinct in man for a wisdom. For example, the father bears the hardship of raising the child and providing for him, and the child remains a dependent upon his father for fifteen years. Were it not that Allah linked offspring to the sexual act and placed in it the pleasure of intercourse, many would have been reluctant to have children. Likewise, the mother bears the hardship of pregnancy, delivery and nursing, etc., to the extent that she may swear during labour that she will never bear again, but when the pain of childbirth passes and the child grows, she longs for another... and so on.

When you contemplate the matter of instinct, you find that the Creator, glory be to Him, placed in man an instinct and its opposite: you find him compassionate in one situation and angry in another, or mighty in one situation and humbled in another. These two instincts do not coexist in man at the same time; the circumstance of faith judges him at one time to be mighty and at another time to be humbled.

Read, if you wish, His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty over the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54].

And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves﴾ [Al-Fath: 29].

So then: the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, placed within you contrasting instincts, He suppresses none of them, but each instinct is to be employed in its appropriate place.

The meaning of ﴿yu'akhidh﴾ [Fatir: 45] is: He punishes and requites. ﴿bima kasabu﴾ [Fatir: 45]: we say kasaba and iktasaba. The word kasaba indicates the presence of a trade in which there is profit and gain over and above the capital, and it indicates the gain that comes naturally. As for iktasaba, it has the form of mufa'alah, which is on the pattern of if'talaja, so it contains artifice and effort.

Therefore the Qur'an uses kasaba for good and iktasaba for evil: ﴿For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 286], because doing good comes from you naturally, with no effort and no artifice, unlike evil, which requires attempts, stratagems, caution and sneaking about, etc.

Therefore we have said: obedience does not cost a person anything, whereas disobedience is what costs a great deal, because obedience comes naturally from you, whereas disobedience requires stratagems, deceit and contrivance.

If you say: what of His saying, the Exalted, concerning evil: ﴿Yes, whoever has earned an evil deed and his sin has encompassed him, those are the companions of the Fire﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 81].

We say: the Qur'an used kasaba with evil because it speaks of those who were extravagant against themselves and went to extremes in disobedience until they loved it and became infatuated with it, and indeed they speak of it and openly display it, and even the disobedience comes from them naturally, as if it were obedience, and they commit it without contrivance or caution. Thus for them it is kasb, not iktisab, and they rejoice in it as if it were gain, so they do not reproach themselves, nor blame themselves, nor repent of their disobedience.

The verse here carries this same meaning: ﴿And if Allah were to take the people to account for what they have earned...﴾ [Fatir: 45], i.e., they have become infatuated with disobedience and wrongdoing and rejoice in it as if it were gain. Then comes the response of the condition: ﴿He would not leave upon its back any creature...﴾ [Fatir: 45]. The meaning of dabbah: everything that crawls upon the earth, that is, that walks upon it at ease; but the word became dominant for that which is ridden and carries loads.

Therefore an Arab said to another: "You have wearied me, O you who go about in youth and in old age, walking at ease."

But, why should beasts bear the consequence of human wrongdoing? They said: The connection here is that the beast is created subjugated for the service and comfort of man, so the destruction of beasts means the cessation of man's comfort, the withholding of rain, the drying up of the earth, and then man cannot find his sustenance, neither from the meat of beasts nor from the plants of the earth. In this is a humbling of man, who sees the means of his living and the causes of his comfort being taken from him without his doing anything, and he is unable to do anything.

When we trace the verses of the Qur'an, we find that it speaks of this meaning in two places:

The first: in Surah An-Nahl: ﴿And if Allah were to take the people to account for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it any creature, but He defers them to a specified term. And when their term comes, they will not remain behind it an hour, nor will they precede it﴾ [An-Nahl: 61].

The other, here in Fatir: ﴿And if Allah were to take the people to account for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back any creature, but He defers them to a specified term. And when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing﴾ [Fatir: 45].

Some may see repetition in the two verses, and far be it from Allah that there be repetition in His speech. If you reflect, you will find a difference between them, giving each its own meaning. The first speaks of the people's wrongdoing, and the other of what they have earned of evil deeds in general. Each of the two expressions gives you a new snapshot, because I may wrong others, but I regret my wrongdoing, do not rejoice in it, and do not persist in it; but if it becomes a habit for me, so that I become infatuated with it, then it is iktisab and artifice in the sense we have mentioned.

The first says: ﴿upon its back﴾ [Fatir: 45] and the other: ﴿upon it﴾ [An-Nahl: 61]. Likewise in the conclusions of the two verses: in the first, the Almighty speaks of the time and the term that neither advances nor delays, and in the other He speaks of recompense, and that Allah is Seeing of the deeds of His servants, nothing of them being hidden from Him. Thus the two verses complement each other, and there is no repetition in them at all.

The pronoun of absence in ﴿upon its back﴾ [Fatir: 45] and ﴿upon it﴾ [An-Nahl: 61] is connected to the verse before it: ﴿...nor is there anything in the heavens or in the earth that could cause Him to fail﴾ [Fatir: 44]. The pronoun refers to the nearest antecedent, which is the earth, and this reference is also understood by the rational context, since the meaning turns toward it.

This verse has for us a story from when we were children in the kuttab of Sheikh Hasan, may Allah have mercy upon him. The Sheikh would assign the 'arif to correct our slates, and on this day Sheikh Hasan sat to correct for us himself. But on this day I had not corrected my slate (and I had got away with it), and I awaited the falaka and the cane (to take effect). But the Sheikh said to me: "Listen, I will teach you how to recite this verse without mixing it with the verse of An-Nahl. Do not combine the two dhaa's nor the two seens," meaning: if you say (bi-zulmihim) do not say (ala zahriha), and if you say (bima kasabu) do not say (la yastakhirun sa'ah), and so on. Thus was our Sheikh, may Allah have mercy upon him, living with the Qur'an and interacting with it, and true is the saying of Allah the Mighty: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [Al-Qamar: 22].

I also had with him, may Allah have mercy upon him, another story, which I still recall, concerning Surah Ash-Shura. The Sheikh sat correcting our slate, and we had fled and had not corrected. When I sat before the Sheikh, I recited (Ha Mim 'Asaq), and we had passed by Ha Mim and Ta Ha and others, but we had not passed by anything like ('Asaq), so I recited it as it is written, 'asaq, and the Sheikh struck me. I recited 'asaq again and he struck me. In the third time he realised that I had not corrected the slate for the 'arif, so he said: "Say: 'ayn, sin, qaf." It has stayed with me ever since, and I have not forgotten it until now. May Allah have mercy upon them and be pleased with them all.

The meaning of the term in ﴿then when their term comes﴾ [Fatir: 45] is: the Resurrection and the punishment, or the term of their annihilation has come with a punishment that uproots them. We know that the punishment of extermination, such as the Cry, the Quake, the Sinking, etc., descends only upon despair of the people's guidance, such that there remains no hope for their life, as came in the story of Prophet Nuh, peace be upon him, when he said: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers﴾ [Nuh: 26-27].

But if there is hope that some of the people will believe, such punishment does not descend upon them.

Or: the term here means the term of the nation, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿For every nation is a term﴾ [Yunus: 49]. So the terms seem to be three: a term for this world, whose end is the establishment of the Hour; a term for the individual, with the end of his lifespan; and a term for the entire nation, when a general punishment comes upon it that destroys them all at once.

Or: for every nation there is a term in which it is victorious and prevails, despite the presence of obstinate ones and disbelievers, as happened to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the Muslims were victorious at Badr. For the nation of oppression and disbelief had a term that ended with Islam and the strength of the Muslims, even though hope was but a glimmer of light, such that despair would prevail over hope.

So much so that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said when it was revealed: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45]. 'Umar said: "What multitude is this, when we are unable to protect ourselves?"

When Badr came and the Muslims were victorious, he said: "Allah has spoken truly: ﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45]." The might of Islam had grown firm, the Muslims had strengthened, and the state of disbelief had been given notice of its end. The term of the disbelieving, wrongdoing nation ended, and the term of the believing nation began.

Therefore, when we contemplate His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor the darknesses and the light, nor the shade and the scorching heat, nor are the living and the dead...﴾ [Fatir: 19-22].

We find four contrasts. The first two correspond to his situation (ﷺ) with his community before the spread of Islam, during the period when paganism dominated the Messenger of Allah and his followers in Makkah: the blind, i.e., the one ignorant of the ruling, and the seeing, the one who knows it; the darknesses, meaning misguidance and disbelief, and the light, which is faith. For they were blind, so Allah willed to give them sight, and they were in the darknesses of ignorance and misguidance, so Allah brought them out of them into the light of faith.

As for the last two contrasts, they correspond to his situation (ﷺ) with his community after Islam had established its pillars and taken firm hold upon the souls of the believers: ﴿nor the shade and the scorching heat, nor are the living and the dead﴾ [Fatir: 21-22]. You see that he began with the attribute of affirmation, and did not say "the scorching heat nor the shade" as he said ﴿the blind and the seeing﴾ [Fatir: 19]. Why? Because the discourse here concerns the nation of victory and the nation of faith, so it was fitting that the contrast begin with the attribute of good that suits this new nation.

In this meaning there is a subtle allusion to the end of the Jahiliyyah and its darknesses and blindness, and an announcement of the beginning of a new term for the nascent nation of faith, which takes shelter in the oasis of faith after Allah gave them life through faith, when they had been dead through disbelief, as He, glory be to Him, said in another verse: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darknesses from which he cannot emerge?﴾ [Al-An'am: 122].

We have previously explained the difference between mayt and mayyit: the mayyit (with shadda) is one whose affair is heading toward death even while he is alive, and among that is the Almighty's address to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ [Az-Zumar: 30], meaning his affair will end in death. As for mayt (without shadda), it is one who has already died.

So then: we can say ﴿then when their term comes﴾ [Fatir: 45], i.e., with the victory of faith over disbelief, ﴿indeed Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing﴾ [Fatir: 45]. The words 'ibad and 'abid are plurals of 'abd, and although both are plurals of one singular, their meanings differ, because the human slave is the property of his master, and as long as he is his property he obeys his commands; whereas the believing person has choice, so Allah addresses him while he may obey or disobey, whereas the slave does not disobey his master if he is a human being.

Yes, he may oppose the command of Allah, but he does not oppose the command of his master. How so? They said: Because Allah is the Forbearing, the Forgiving; whereas a human master is not free from tyranny, arrogance, or domination and oppression.

There is a difference between the obedience of a slave who is free to disobey and his obedience while he is compelled to obey. We previously illustrated this matter with two slaves, Sa'id and Sa'd. Sa'id is bound to his master with a chain from which he cannot escape, and Sa'd is set free, bound by nothing. When the master calls one of them, he comes. Which of them is more obedient? There is no doubt that Sa'd is more obedient than Sa'id, because he comes to his master while he is able and free not to come, whereas Sa'id can only respond, for if he disobeyed, the master would pull him by the chain.

Thus Allah, glory be to Him, created creatures with the power of choice and set for them this rule: ﴿Whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]. Whoever wills obeys, and whoever wills disobeys. This is how servants behave toward their master. If the servant says: "O Lord, You created me, provided for me, gave me my limbs, and made me one who chooses, and I am one of Your servants. Therefore I surrender my choice to Your choice and my will to Your will," then this servant has chosen to be subdued to his Lord and made subservient, just as the heavens and the earth were made subservient.

These are the ('ibad) servants, the elite of creation, who preferred God's will over their own wills. For this reason, the Almighty speaks of them and gives us a picture of them: ﴿The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan: 63], meaning: humble, not arrogant. And what is there to be arrogant about? ﴿Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], nor will you reach the mountains in height﴾ [al-Isra: 37]. ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace." And those who spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing. And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is ever adhering. Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence." And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever, between that, moderate. And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ [al-Furqan: 63–68].

These are eight qualities that draw for us a complete picture of those who deserved to be the servants of Allah. For this reason, their Lord addresses them elsewhere: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ [al-Zumar: 53].

Among Allah's mercy to His servants is that good deeds erase evil deeds, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud: 114]. Greater than this, Allah's mercy does not stop at erasing the evil deed; rather, after repentance, the evil deed is changed into a good deed: ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan: 70].

Regarding the meaning of (عباد) and (عبيد) which we have clarified, we have heard someone object and say: "The Qur'an contains something that contradicts this meaning, namely His saying, in the context of the Day of Resurrection, addressing the leaders and masters who misled people and made disbelief appealing to them: ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ [al-Furqan: 17]."

We say: there is no contradiction between the verses as you claim, because the discussion here concerns the Hereafter, and in the Hereafter there is no choice. So there is no difference between (عباد) and (عبيد) in the Hereafter.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Seeing of His servants﴾ [Fatir: 45], He mentions here the attribute of sight, because it is the strongest means of knowledge and perception. Knowledge has several means, which the Almighty mentioned in His saying: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts, that you might be grateful﴾ [al-Nahl: 78].

Hearing is the first means of perception, and it is the first limb to awaken and carry out its function in the newborn. The proof is that if you place, for example, your finger in front of his eye, he does not blink; but if you shout in his ear, he is startled and responds to the sound. Hearing is also the faculty that is never inactive during sleep, because through it summoning takes place. Hearing is the first means for values and immaterial matters, and through it a person receives the method of Allah.

As for sight, although it comes in second place, it is greater than hearing and stronger, because you may hear about a thing without paying attention to it. But if you move from hearing to sight, you have reached the peak of perception about which there is no doubt. For this reason they say: "There is no 'where' from seeing with the eye." What you hear about may be false, but what you see is never anything but true.

Therefore, when the Almighty wants to confirm a piece of information for us, He says: ﴿Have you not seen﴾ [al-Zumar: 21], because what the eye sees is the most emphatic. Abu Ja'far, when he said to Muqatil, "Admonish me, O Muqatil," Muqatil replied: "Shall I admonish you with what I have heard, or with what I have perhaps seen?" "By Allah, answer me: which of the two?" He said: "Admonish me with what you have seen." Yes, because you may hear falsehood, but if you see with your own eyes, it is the truth.
